source: Existing database descriptions; editorial changes do not certify venue facts or safety.

changes.name: Berghain
changes.before: Berghain: The high priestess of techno and the ultimate queer pilgrimage. This industrial temple is world-renowned for its uncompromising sound, legendary Sunday sessions, and a sanctuary of pure hedonism. Inside, the world disappears—no phones, no mirrors, just raw energy across the Berghain floor, Panorama Bar, and the hidden darkrooms. It’s not just a club; it’s a weekend-long rite of passage. ⛓️🖤🔥Pro Tips for the Pilgrimage:The Look: There’s no "right" outfit, but authenticity is key. Dark, queer, fetish, or creative looks usually vibe best. Avoid looking like a tourist—wear something you can dance in for 12+ hours.The Vibe: Know who is playing. The bouncers want to see that you’re there for the music and the community, not just to sightsee.The Wait: Be prepared for the "Berghain Snake" (the line). Sunday mornings/afternoons are peak queer hours and often have the best energy.The Rule: Once inside, stickers go on cameras. Respect the privacy of the space—what happens in Berghain, stays in Berghain.
changes.after: Berghain is an electronic music club with the main Berghain floor, Panorama Bar and darkrooms. Long weekend sessions are part of its programme. Photography is prohibited and entry is at the door staff's discretion; check the lineup and current entry guidance before going.

changes.name: Prinzknecht
changes.before: Schöneberg’s ruggedly handsome powerhouse. 🇩🇪 This spacious, high-ceilinged haunt is the gold standard for the "grown-up" queer scene. Think exposed brick, industrial vibes, and a massive bar that’s always buzzing. Whether you’re here for the legendary Sunday coffee and cake or a stiff evening cocktail, it’s the place to see and be seen in the gayborhood. 🧱🍸✨
changes.after: Prinzknecht is a spacious gay bar in Schöneberg, with exposed brick, high ceilings and a large central bar. The programme includes Sunday coffee and cake alongside evening drinks.

changes.name: Möbel-Olfe
changes.before: Tucked away in the raw, concrete underbelly of a 1960s housing estate at the chaotic crossroads of Kottbusser Tor, Möbel-Olfe is Kreuzberg’s legendary, high-ceilinged "Trinkhalle" (drinking hall) that serves absolute queer baseline excellence. Retaining the name and gritty skeleton of the early 20th-century furniture showroom it once was, this unpretentious matrix features a wild, shifting landscape of improvised decor—including real grass nailed to the walls, disco balls, and retro wooden chairs glued upside down to the ceiling. It completely discards the hyper-polished tourist pretense of Mitte, choosing instead to blast out hi-NRG, synth wave, and retro disco sets while throwing back crisp Polish lagers and stiff vodkas.
changes.after: Möbel-Olfe is a queer bar at Kottbusser Tor in a former furniture showroom. Upside-down chairs, disco balls and improvised wall decorations give the room its character. The music includes hi-NRG, synth-pop and disco.

changes.name: Roses Bar
changes.before: Roses: A kitschy, neon-pink wonderland in the heart of Kreuzberg. 🇩🇪 With furry walls, flashing Madonnas, and leopard prints, this legendary spot is a visual sensory overload. It’s a tiny, high-energy sanctuary that’s an absolute must for a wild pre-club drink or a late-night disco session. 💖✨🍿
changes.after: Roses Bar is a small Kreuzberg bar with pink furry walls, leopard print and illuminated religious figures. Disco music and dense decoration make it a lively option for a drink before or after a club night.

changes.name: Der Boiler
changes.before: Berlin’s ultimate steam-powered sanctuary. 🇩🇪 This massive, award-winning gay sauna is the gold standard for wellness and cruising. Spread across multiple levels with sleek industrial design, it features a massive sauna, steam rooms, a whirlpool, and plenty of dark corners for exploration. It’s clean, professional, and undeniably hot. 🧖‍♂️⛓️🔥
changes.after: Der Boiler is a gay sauna spread across several levels, with sauna and steam rooms, a whirlpool and cruising areas. Its industrial interior combines wellness facilities with spaces for socialising and adult encounters.

changes.name: Mutschmann's
changes.before: The undisputed temple of leather and rubber. 🇩🇪 Located in the heart of Schöneberg, this men-only institution is a dark, intense, and uncompromising sanctuary for the fetish community. It’s where gear is the law, and the atmosphere is thick with masculine energy and heavy cruising. ⛓️🖤🔥
changes.after: Mutschmann's is a men-only fetish and cruising venue in Schöneberg, with a focus on leather and rubber. Clothing requirements depend on the event, so read the current dress code before visiting.

changes.name: Vabali Spa
changes.before: A Balinese dreamscape in the heart of Berlin. 🇩🇪 While not exclusively queer, this massive 20,000sqm textile-free sanctuary is a total magnet for the community. With bamboo huts, infinity pools, and a labyrinth of saunas, it’s the ultimate "reset button" for your Berlin weekend. Pure luxury, total nudity, and zero judgment. 🌿🧖‍♂️✨
changes.after: Vabali Spa is a large, Balinese-inspired textile-free spa in Berlin, with pools, bamboo buildings and several saunas. It is a general spa rather than a dedicated LGBTQ+ venue.

changes.name: HAFEN
changes.before: The beating heart of Schöneberg’s gayborhood. 🏳️‍🌈A legendary local institution where kitsch meets class. From cozy nooks and daily happy hours to wild Schlager nights and the iconic Sunday "Drama" disco, it’s the ultimate living room for Berlin’s queer community. Unpretentious, vibrant, and always full of heart. ✨⚓
changes.after: HAFEN is a gay bar in Schöneberg with a programme that includes Schlager nights and the Sunday Drama disco. The smaller seating areas offer somewhere to sit between drinks and dancing.

changes.name: Blond
changes.before: Schöneberg’s pink-powered paradise! 🇩🇪 A cozy, kitschy café by day and a high-energy cocktail bar by night. With over 50 cocktails on the menu and a vibe that’s pure "retro-fabulous," it’s the perfect spot to start your night with a glittery bang. 💖🍸✨
changes.after: Blond operates as a café during the day and a cocktail bar in the evening in Schöneberg. Pink decor, a retro interior and an extensive cocktail menu shape the setting.

changes.name: Heile Welt
changes.before: Welcome to Heile Welt, Berlin’s ultimate, neon-laced "queer living room" where classic Schöneberg kiez charm gets a wonderfully vibrant modern glow-up. Nestled directly inside the historic Regenbogen-Kiez near Nollendorfplatz, this cozy, narrow lounge effortlessly bridges the gap between intimate conversation and late-night party chaos. Step past the signature blue neon awning to find a multi-room setup adorned with rich purple color accents, velvet-textured seating, and a dedicated indoor smoking lounge.
changes.after: Heile Welt is a narrow Schöneberg lounge near Nollendorfplatz, recognisable by its blue neon sign. Inside are several rooms with purple accents, upholstered seating and a separate smoking lounge.

changes.name: Dreizehn
changes.before: The cozy alternative to Schöneberg’s loud basslines. 🇩🇪 A "pub-style" sanctuary where classic gay hits float through the air and the vibe is always warm. It’s intimate, relaxed, and a favorite for a more mature crowd looking for genuine conversation over a wide range of spirits. 🍻✨
changes.after: Dreizehn is a small, pub-style gay bar in Schöneberg. Classic pop plays in the background, and the listing describes a largely mature crowd who come for drinks and conversation.

changes.name: K6
changes.before: The friendly neighborhood staple. 🇩🇪 Located just steps from Nollendorfplatz, this long-standing gem is all about that local, lived-in charm. Whether you’re soaking up the sun in their huge beer garden or hitting the dance floor for German pop and Schlager hits, it’s a welcoming spot for every tribe. Unpretentious, cozy, and famously fun. 🍻🕺✨
changes.after: K6 is a neighbourhood gay bar near Nollendorfplatz. It has a beer garden and a dance floor, with German pop and Schlager among the music played.

changes.name: Tramp's
changes.before: Step into Tramp's, Berlin’s ultimate, cave-like 24-hour gay refuge hidden right in the historic, beating heart of the Schöneberg gay village. Originally a traditional Irish pub reimagined in 2003 as a cozy neighborhood dive sanctuary, this unpretentious stronghold completely treats bedtime like a purely optional suggestion. The interior serves a gritty, tile-fragment ruins aesthetic paired with softly clicking slot machines, indoor smoking, and exceptionally cheap pours. Complete with a private, low-light backroom and darkroom area tailored for jeans, leather, and fetish enthusiasts, it is a delightfully relaxed, judgement-free zone where neighborhood weirdos, mature regulars, and weary travelers come to drink, decompress, or slide into some raw after-hours cruising.
changes.after: Tramp's is a gay bar in Schöneberg with a tiled interior, slot machines and indoor smoking. It also has a backroom and darkroom, with jeans, leather and fetish wear part of the setting.

changes.name: Romeo & Romeo
changes.before: The heart of Schöneberg’s cafe culture. 🇩🇪 This corner gem is the perfect spot to start your day or refuel during a gallery stroll. Known for its delicious breakfast spreads, friendly baristas, and a vibe that’s pure "neighborhood love," it’s a community staple where the local queer scene meets for coffee and gossip. ☕🥐✨
changes.after: Romeo & Romeo is a corner café in Schöneberg serving breakfast, coffee and pastries. Its location among the neighbourhood's queer venues makes it a daytime meeting point.

changes.name: Kurhaus Korsakow
changes.before: Friedrichshain’s cozy-cool living room. 🇩🇪 Located right on the vibrant Boxhagener Platz, this place is the definition of "Kiez-chic." With high ceilings, vintage chandeliers, and a massive terrace, it’s the ultimate queer-friendly spot for a long, boozy brunch or a rustic German dinner. Relaxed, inclusive, and effortlessly stylish. 🛋️🍳✨
changes.after: Kurhaus Korsakow is on Boxhagener Platz in Friedrichshain. High ceilings, vintage chandeliers and a large terrace frame a menu of brunch dishes and German food.

changes.name: Sissi
changes.before: An Austrian fairytale in the heart of Schöneberg. 🇩🇪 Step into this regal, rose-colored dream for the ultimate "Sissi Empress" experience. It’s a cozy, queer-popular café serving up authentic schnitzel, divine cakes, and Viennese charm. Classy, camp, and deliciously nostalgic. 🍰👑✨
changes.after: Sissi is an Austrian café and restaurant in Schöneberg, with rose-coloured decor. Schnitzel and cakes are among the dishes described in the listing.

changes.name: Südblock
changes.before: The big, queer heart of Kottbusser Tor. 🇩🇪 This isn't just a bar; it’s a community powerhouse. With its massive terrace overlooking the gritty charm of Kotti, Südblock is a vibrant mix of Turkish brunch, political activism, drag bingo, and sweaty dance nights. It’s inclusive, loud, and unapologetically Kreuzberg. 🏳️‍🌈✊✨
changes.after: Südblock combines a café, bar and cultural programme at Kottbusser Tor. Its large terrace and events ranging from political discussions to drag bingo and dance nights connect it to Kreuzberg's queer community.

changes.name: Boyberry Berlin
changes.before: Boyberry Berlin is the unapologetic, high-energy successor to the legendary Tom’s Bar, bringing a sleek Spanish edge to the heart of Schöneberg’s historic rainbow district. It’s a multi-story playground that perfectly captures the "sex-positive and liberated" spirit of the city.The VibeModern Meets Cruisy: Gone is the "clone-era" leather aesthetic of its predecessor; Boyberry is redesigned with a brighter, more vibrant look while keeping things strictly "men-only" and wildly playful.Youthful Energy: While the crowd is diverse, it’s a major magnet for a younger, adventurous generation looking for a mix of social drinks and late-night connections.The Layout: The ground floor is a stylish social bar where you can sip cocktails and scan the room. Once you’re ready to dive deeper, head into the massive cruising zone—it's packed with private cabins, a maze, dark rooms, and glory holes. ⛓️🖤✨
changes.after: Boyberry Berlin occupies the former Tom's Bar site in Schöneberg. The men-only venue combines a ground-floor social bar with cruising areas, private cabins, darkrooms and a maze on other levels.

changes.name: Rauschgold
changes.before: Rauschgold is Kreuzberg drag-pop chaos done right: karaoke spikes, camp performance energy, and a crowd that loves singalong catharsis as much as flirting. If you want Berlin to feel messy, theatrical, and very alive without pretending to be too cool, this is your room.
changes.after: Rauschgold is a Kreuzberg bar centred on drag, karaoke and pop music. Performances and singalongs are part of its programme; check the current listings for the night's format.

changes.name: Centralhjørnet
changes.before: Centralhjørnet: Step into history, honey! 🇩🇰 As the world’s oldest gay bar, it’s a legendary mix of old-school hygge and over-the-top camp. Famous for its wild seasonal decor and a crowd that’s as diverse as a pride parade. Grab a beer, feel the history, and soak up the glitter. 🍻✨
changes.after: Centralhjørnet is a long-running gay bar in Copenhagen with seasonal decorations and a camp pub atmosphere. Beer and conversation are central to the setting.

changes.name: MEN's Bar
changes.before: The ultimate leather and denim playground. 🇩🇰 No fluff, just pure masculine energy, cheap beer, and a legendary darkroom. Whether you're in gear or just gear-curious, it’s the go-to spot for a raw, cruising-friendly night in the heart of Copenhagen. ⛓️🍻
changes.after: MEN's Bar is a gay bar with a leather and denim focus in central Copenhagen. It combines drinks with a darkroom and an adult cruising setting.

changes.name: Jailhouse CPH
changes.before: Get locked up in the best way possible! 🇩🇰 This police-themed basement is a Copenhagen legend. From prison-cell booths to bartenders in uniform, it’s the ultimate spot for strong cocktails and a playful, cruising-friendly vibe. Guilty of being a damn good time. ⛓️👮‍♂️✨
changes.after: Jailhouse CPH is a police-themed basement bar in Copenhagen, with booths styled as prison cells and staff uniforms. Cocktails and an informal social atmosphere are part of the concept.

changes.name: DAS (Den Anden Side)
changes.before: DAS Copenhagen: The undisputed crown jewel of Scandinavian queer techno. 🇩🇰 This is more than a club—it’s a high-octane sanctuary for queer culture where the underground truly breathes. 🖤⛓️The vibe shifts with the moon: some nights are strictly legendary gay parties, while others open up to a curated mixed crowd of electronic disciples. But don't just show up—know the code. Their door policy is fierce, rooted in a rock-solid awareness culture. It’s all about consent, respect, and protecting the space. Dress to express, respect the vibe, and lose yourself in the heavy, avant-garde beats. Pure liberation, no apologies. Strict no-photo policy (stickers on cameras!) 🔥✨
changes.after: Den Anden Side is an electronic music club in Copenhagen with queer-focused and mixed-crowd events. The programme varies by night. Check its consent, entry and no-photography policies before attending.

changes.name: Rust
changes.before: The beating heart of Nørrebro. A legendary multi-story haunt where raw indie clashes with bold hip-hop and relentless techno marathons. With a progressive crowd and a dancefloor that never quits, this is authentic queer-coded club culture. Raw, real, and ready for you. ✨🔥
changes.after: Rust is a multi-storey music venue in Nørrebro. Its programme spans indie, hip-hop and electronic music, so the lineup is a better guide to the evening than a single club label.

changes.name: Amigo Sauna
changes.before: Three floors of pure, steamy bliss in the heart of Copenhagen.  From relaxing sauna sessions to private cabins and a buzzing cinema, it’s the city’s go-to spot for men to unwind and connect. Classic,  in a need of renovations but always cruising-friendly. 🧖‍♂️✨
changes.after: Amigo Sauna is a multi-level gay sauna in central Copenhagen, with sauna facilities, private cabins and a cinema. It combines bathing facilities with adult cruising areas.

changes.name: Scandinavian Leather Men (SLM) Copenhagen
changes.before: 🏳️‍🌈SLM Copenhagen is the ultimate high-octane sanctuary for the leather and fetish community in Scandinavia. Tucked away in a discrete basement in the city center, this member-only club is a multi-room playground for men who want to explore their darkest desires in a safe, respectful, and strictly coded environment. From the heavy-duty play equipment to the steamy cruising areas and the well-stocked bar, SLM serves pure masculine energy. Whether it's a "Naked Night," a "Uniform Party," or the legendary "Yellow Night," it’s the place where the gear comes out and the inhibitions stay at the door.
changes.after: SLM Copenhagen is a members' club for men interested in leather and fetish culture. Its basement premises include a bar, play equipment and cruising areas. Themed events have specific membership and clothing requirements.

changes.name: Body Bio
changes.before: Copenhagen’s classic cinematic hideaway. A long-standing staple for the community, offering private cabins, cinema screens, and a relaxed cruising vibe. It’s low-key, authentic, and perfect for those looking to disconnect and explore in peace. 🎬✨
changes.after: Body Bio is an adult cinema and cruising venue in Copenhagen, with private cabins and screening rooms. It offers a smaller-scale setting than a nightclub.

changes.name: Axel Hotel Berlin
changes.before: The "hetero-friendly" palace of Schöneberg. 🇩🇪 Located just steps from the Wittenbergplatz, this sleek, design-forward hotel is a true queer landmark. With its golden facade, rooftop spa, and a vibe that screams "sexy sophistication," it’s the place to stay if you want to be right in the heart of the action while surrounded by luxury. 🏨✨🥂
changes.after: Axel Hotel Berlin is a design hotel near Wittenbergplatz in Schöneberg, marketed to LGBTQ+ travellers. A gold-coloured façade and rooftop spa are among its features, with local gay bars nearby.

changes.name: ArtHotel Connection
changes.before: ArtHotel Connection: The heart of Schöneberg with an artistic soul. 🇩🇪 Located in a beautiful 19th-century Art Nouveau building, this boutique hotel is a beloved queer staple. It’s unpretentious, uniquely decorated, and sits right above some of Berlin's most iconic gay bars. Pure "home away from home" vibes. 🏨🎨✨
changes.after: ArtHotel Connection is a boutique hotel in a 19th-century Art Nouveau building in Schöneberg. Individually decorated rooms and its location above local gay bars give it a close connection to the neighbourhood's nightlife.

changes.name: Mercure Hotel Berlin Zentrum
changes.before: The "Gift to the Gay Ghetto." 🇩🇪 It’s nothing fancy, but the location is unbeatable. Situated right on Fuggerstraße, you are practically inside the bars before you even leave the lobby. Reliable, central, and totally unpretentious. 🍻⛓️✨
changes.after: Mercure Hotel Berlin Zentrum is on Fuggerstraße in Schöneberg, close to the neighbourhood's gay bars. Its location suits visitors who want to explore the area on foot.

changes.name: Patricia
changes.before: S/S Patricia (commonly known just as Patricia) is Stockholm's legendary, floating party vessel and one of the longest-running fixtures of the city's LGBTQ+ nightlife. Permanently moored along the Södermalm waterfront, this historic 1930s former British naval ship transforms every Sunday night into a massive, multi-dancefloor queer club night
changes.after: S/S Patricia is a permanently moored former ship on Stockholm's Södermalm waterfront. Its Sunday LGBTQ+ club nights use several dance floors, giving the venue a different rhythm from its other evenings.

changes.name: Why Not
changes.before: Why Not Vienna is the glittering, time-tested grand dame of the Austrian capital's LGBTQ+ nightlife. Holding down the crown as Vienna’s absolute oldest running gay and queer discotheque since opening its legendary doors in 1980, this multi-tiered sanctuary is a vibrant right of passage tucked right into the city's historic first district. Spread across three distinct structural floors and triple-stocked bars, the vibe here is a shameless, energetic celebration of life. It smoothly moves from relaxed, intimate drink chatter on the ground level to high-octane pop anthems, trashy club classics, and electric house beats down on the main dancefloor.
changes.after: Why Not is a gay and queer club in Vienna's first district, operating since 1980. Several floors and bars connect an upstairs space for drinks with a main dance floor playing pop, house and club classics.

changes.name: Village Bar
changes.before: Village Bar is the high-energy, neon-drenched neighborhood anchor that has been shining as one of Vienna's absolute brightest stars right next to the historic Naschmarkt since 2005. Reimagined with a sleek post-lockdown design upgrade, this compact, cozy social hive packs a massive punch by squeezing video walls, stellar pop music tracks, and an unbelievably lively party energy into a tight, intimate floor layout. It trades overwhelming, cavernous dancefloor posturing for pure, unadulterated neighborhood camaraderie, serving as an air-conditioned, ice-cold summer escape where meeting someone new over a perfectly mixed cocktail is practically unavoidable
changes.after: Village Bar is a small Vienna bar near Naschmarkt, with video walls, pop music and an air-conditioned interior. The compact layout puts the focus on drinks and socialising rather than a large dance floor.

changes.name: Le Belgica
changes.before: Le Belgica is a fiercely unapologetic, delightfully compact Brussels institution that has been anchoring the city’s Saint-Jacques gay quarter since the mid-1800s. This is raw, vintage bar realness at its finest—boasting a wonderfully distressed, rock-and-roll interior where neon lights catch spinning disco balls and eccentric decor. There are no umbrellas in the drinks or sanitized lounge pop here; instead, you dive straight into a thick, pulsing room fueled by high-energy live resident DJs spinning tech, deep, and acid house. It is the ultimate, high-spirited pre-club landing pad where the signature, secret-recipe semi-frozen "Belgica" cocktail packs a serious punch.
changes.after: Le Belgica is a compact gay bar in Brussels' Saint-Jacques quarter, with a worn-in interior, disco balls and neon lighting. Resident DJs play house, and the bar serves a semi-frozen Belgica cocktail.

changes.name: Station BXL
changes.before: Station BXL is the ultimate, high-energy launchpad of Brussels’ historic Saint-Jacques gay village. Located a mere stiletto throw from the Grand Place on the iconic Rue du Marché au Charbon, this vibrant, neon-tinted hotspot functions as the perfect hybrid between a cozy daytime lounge and a buzzing pre-club party train station. During the late afternoon, you can relax on their spacious outdoor sidewalk terrace, sipping local Belgian craft beers while retro 80s and 90s music videos flash across multiple screens.
changes.after: Station BXL is a bar on Rue du Marché au Charbon near the Grand Place. A pavement terrace, Belgian beers and screens showing music videos make it a daytime and early-evening meeting place before clubbing.

changes.name: Cox
changes.before: Welcome to the undisputed, heavy-hitting crown jewel of the Marais sidewalk scene. Operating since 1995 under the fierce battle cry "Rouge Toujours" (Always Red), COX is a legendary Parisian institution recognizable from a block away by its glowing red lighting and the massive, high-energy wall of people spilling past its tiny chain ropes directly onto the pavement. It splits its soul between a packed, raw industrial interior featuring a rotating theme art layout every three months and a chaotic, hyper-social outdoor terrace. There is zero pretense here—it functions as the ultimate, bass-heavy house music melting pot where the drinks flow fast and eye contact is a local sport.
changes.after: COX is a gay bar in Le Marais, recognisable by its red lighting and street-side crowd. The industrial-style interior has changing art displays, with house music and an outdoor terrace area.

changes.name: Banana Café
changes.before: Say hello to the eccentric, neon-yellow matriarch of late-night Parisian camp. Established all the way back in 1990, Banana Café is a legendary, tropical-themed gay institution parked right in the buzzing heart of Châtelet—safely outside the usual Marais circuit. This place doesn’t take itself seriously, blanketing its multi-floor layout in faux palm trees, jungle decor, and kitschy neon. It’s a beautifully chaotic hybrid: a relaxed outdoor sidewalk terrace for afternoon people-watching that transforms by night into a high-energy house music club, complete with drag extravaganzas, karaoke sets, cabaret, and the historic distinction of being the first Parisian venue to introduce go-go dancer shows.
changes.after: Banana Café is a tropical-themed gay bar near Châtelet, with palm-tree decor and neon lighting. A pavement terrace offers afternoon drinks, while the evening programme includes house music, drag, karaoke and cabaret.

changes.name: Bootshaus
changes.before: Bootshaus is the absolute heavyweight champion of Cologne’s club scene and a world-class temple for electronic music—voted the #1 club in Germany and #5 globally in 2025. While it’s not a dedicated gay club, it serves major queer energy by playing host to the most legendary LGBTQ+ events in Europe, like the high-production SEXY Party and the fetish-fueled KitKatClub takeovers from Berlin. Housed in a former shipyard, it’s a raw, industrial labyrinth where the sound system will literally rattle your soul.
changes.after: Bootshaus is an electronic music club in a former Cologne shipyard. It is not a dedicated gay venue, but its programme includes LGBTQ+ events such as SEXY Party and KitKatClub takeovers. Check the current lineup for the event's format.

changes.name: ExCorner
changes.before: ExCorner is the  "everyone knows your name" sanctuary of Cologne’s gayborhood. Known as the heart and soul of Schaafenstraße, this corner pub serves major "shabby-chic" energy with its rustic wooden interior and legendary disco ball. It’s a high-vibes melting pot where long-time locals, young party-seekers, and tourists mingle over cold Kölsch. Whether it's the high-energy Street Party during Pride or just a Tuesday night where the pop anthems are hitting just right, ExCorner is unpretentious, loud, and unapologetically queer.
changes.after: ExCorner is a gay corner pub on Cologne's Schaafenstraße, with a wooden interior and a disco ball. Kölsch, pop music and street-side gatherings connect it to the neighbourhood's bar scene.

changes.name: Club NYX
changes.before: Club NYX is a multi-story, neon-soaked playground named after the Greek goddess of the night. Rising from the ashes of the legendary gay disco Exit, this former carriage house is a sprawling, chaotic wonderland of self-expression where safety and inclusion are served alongside heavy bass. Spread across three distinct floors connected by a maze of stairs, each room offers an entirely different vibe.
changes.after: Club NYX is an Amsterdam nightclub in a former carriage house, named after the Greek goddess of the night. Three floors offer different music and settings, connected by a network of stairs.

changes.name: Trumps
changes.before: As the crown jewel of Portugal's queer nightlife for over 45 years, Trumps is giving iconic legacy with a futuristic glow-up. Located in the heart of the trendy Príncipe Real district, this isn't just a club; it’s a sprawling 1,500m² sanctuary where "freedom is lived on the dancefloor." Expect a neon-drenched aesthetic, disco balls galore, and a state-of-the-art LED wall that serves pure digital fantasy. The atmosphere is unapologetically inclusive—a "come as you are" megaspace where the sexiest bartenders in town serve looks and cocktails with equal flair.
changes.after: Trumps is a queer nightclub in Lisbon's Príncipe Real district. Neon lighting, disco balls and an LED wall frame a large dance space. Check the current programme for its parties, performers and admission details.

changes.name: Finalmente Club
changes.before: Finalmente Club is the undisputed, fierce matriarch of Lisbon’s queer nightlife. Throwing open its hidden doors in 1976—just two years after Portugal broke free from dictatorship—this tiny, legendary institution is affectionately revered as the national "cathedral of transformismo" (drag and cabaret art). It is the longest-running LGBTQIA+ refuge in the city and has spent half a century serving unadulterated lip-sync divinity. Free from commercial pretension, it splits its magic into a cozy early-evening café concert salon and a late-night subterranean dance pit.
changes.after: Finalmente Club is a small Lisbon venue for drag and cabaret, operating since 1976. Its café-concert setting shifts into a later dance programme, with lip-sync performance central to its identity.

changes.name: Punto BCN
changes.before: Punto BCN is the undisputed, historic grandfather of Gaixample nightlife. Thrown wide open back in March 1990, this grand, brightly lit, and multi-level institution completely reshaped Barcelona's queer landscape by trading the secretive, dark, and closeted window shutters of the past for an expansive, unpretentious meeting ground. It functions as the ultimate community living room rather than a hyper-curated techno cave. Inside its airy layout, you'll find a massive ground-floor bar, a bustling pool table, and an upstairs lounge meant for actual, real conversations before the midnight club migrations hit. As the original crown jewel of the local nightlife giant Grupo Arena, it operates as the neighborhood’s essential launchpad, frequently handing out free entry wristbands or heavy drink discounts for their late-night mega-clubs.
changes.after: Punto BCN is a gay bar in Barcelona's Gaixample district, operating since 1990. A ground-floor bar, pool table and upstairs lounge provide space for drinks and conversation before the later club hours.

changes.name: Mantrix Club
changes.before: Mantrix (often referred to as Matrix by visitors) is the high-octane "late-night ritual" of Gran Canaria’s queer scene. Tucked away on the 4th floor of the iconic Yumbo Centre, it’s the island's most popular gay disco where the party only truly ignites when the rest of the center starts to wind down. This sanctuary serves major main-character energy with its world-class international house music, state-of-the-art sound system, and a dark, adventurous cruising area featuring cabins for those looking to turn the heat all the way up.
changes.after: Mantrix is a late-night gay club on the upper level of Gran Canaria's Yumbo Centre. House music leads the programme, with a dance floor and a separate cruising area with cabins.

changes.name: Eagle London
changes.before: Nestled under the Victorian railway arches of Vauxhall, The Eagle is giving "industrial-chic meets bearded bliss." This isn't your average polished cocktail lounge; it’s a raw, high-energy sanctuary where leather, denim, and glitter coexist in perfect harmony. The vibe is unapologetically masculine yet fiercely inclusive, shifting from a relaxed neighborhood haunt during the week to a sweat-soaked, high-octane dance floor on the weekends. With its famous outdoor garden terrace and a "no-attitude" policy, it’s the ultimate "chosen family" hub for those who like their nights out with a bit of grit and a lot of soul. (Pro Tip: If you want the peak Eagle experience, Horse Meat Disco Sundays are mandatory. The queue starts early, so get there by 9:00 PM to ensure you’re on the floor when the glitter balls start spinning. Also, check their schedule for Duckie—a long-running, eccentric Saturday night of "post-gay" performance art and dance!)
changes.after: Eagle London is a Vauxhall gay bar with a garden terrace and a programme spanning social evenings, performance and dancing. The listing includes Horse Meat Disco and other recurring events; check the current calendar rather than relying on a fixed weekly schedule.

changes.name: The Basement Club at Legends
changes.before: The Basement Club at Legends is Brighton's favorite subterranean queer playground, tucked away right beneath the main hotel and bar. Sweaty, sexy, and packed to the brim, this cavernous space is where the night truly escalates. Once the ground-floor cabaret wrap up, the crowd migrates downward into a beautifully intense vortex of shifting neon lights, pumping sound systems, and pure high-energy dance floor euphoria. From upfront dance anthems to shamelessly fun pop mashups mixing Beyoncé with Blondie, it is the quintessential dark, loud, and liberating late-night safe space.
changes.after: The Basement Club at Legends is beneath the hotel and bar in Brighton. Its downstairs dance floor follows the upstairs cabaret, with dance tracks and pop mashups in a louder late-night setting.

changes.name: G-A-Y Manchester
changes.before: Right in the heart of Manchester's world-famous Gay Village, G-A-Y Manchester is giving unapologetic bubblegum-pop realness. It is a two-floor sanctuary of pink neon, mirrored walls, and screens blasting the latest chart-topping music videos alongside iconic throwback anthems. The vibe is energetic, vibrant, and fiercely commercial, making it the ultimate destination for those who want to "dance like nobody's watching" to pure pop bliss. Whether you're catching a RuPaul's Drag Race UK star on stage or soaking in the sun on the outdoor terrace, it’s a "main character energy" hub that has been a cornerstone of Canal Street life since the early 2000s. Pro Tip: This is the best place to snag discounted entry wristbands for late-night clubs in the Village. Also, keep an eye out for their themed Y2K nights—they are legendary for noughties nostalgia and killer drag sets. If the main floor is too packed, the outdoor terrace is a prime spot for a mid-pop breather and some world-class people-watching.
changes.after: G-A-Y Manchester is a multi-level bar in the Gay Village with pink neon, mirrors and music-video screens. The programme focuses on pop, themed nights and drag appearances, with an outdoor terrace for a break from the main room.

changes.name: Eagle Manchester
changes.before: Welcome to Manchester's ultimate underground temple of masculine leather, kink, and testosterone. Awarded the prestigious X Awards 2024 Bar of the Year, The Eagle Bar (historically modeled after the legendary global Eagle brand) is the absolute crowning capital of Manchester's fetish subculture. Located inside a historic, beautifully converted Victorian warehouse on Bloom Street, the interior drops standard commercial glitter for a dark, moody Steampunk-meets-industrial layout. The venue flawlessly splits its identity: the main social bar upfront pays homage to the city’s industrial roots with plush seating and heavy brick, while the back—specifically known as The Black Eagle—plunges you into a pitch-black, neon-rimmed, heavy-duty cruising area and darkroom arena rigged for absolute physical freedom. It is intense, uninhibited, beautifully grimy, and Universally known as the premier sanctuary for men to completely shed their corporate armor.
changes.after: Eagle Manchester is a gay bar in a converted Victorian warehouse on Bloom Street. A brick-lined social bar connects to The Black Eagle, a darker cruising area. Check the event listing for themed nights and any clothing requirements.

changes.name: Coming Out
changes.before: Coming Out is the undisputed, holy matriarch of Rome’s "Gay Street". Holding its crown since 2001, this legendary bistro-bar sits literally a stone’s throw from the ancient Colosseum. By day, it's a sunny, relaxed spot serving up breakfast and plates of pasta; by night, the mood drops into pure camp theatricality. With a weekly lineup packed with drag bingo, fierce karaoke, and late-night DJ sets, it functions as the vibrant, beating heart of local queer street life. Stepping out onto the pavement with a cocktail to be confronted by a glittering, ancient Roman monument is a spiritual rite of passage.
changes.after: Coming Out is a bistro-bar on Rome's Gay Street near the Colosseum. Daytime service includes breakfast and pasta, while the evening programme features drag bingo, karaoke and DJ sets.

changes.name: Muccassassina
changes.before: Muccassassina is Italy’s ultimate, iconic queer nightlife extravaganza. Born in the early '90s to bankroll the Circolo di Cultura Omosessuale Mario Mieli (a legendary local LGBTQIA+ rights group), this party has spent over three decades serving pure, unfiltered clubbing divinity. It’s a multi-story hedonistic rabbit warren of mind-blowing drag shows, fierce choreography, and high-energy house, pop, and techno beats that will leave you absolutely breathless
changes.after: Muccassassina is a Rome queer party with roots in fundraising for the Mario Mieli LGBTQIA+ cultural organisation. Drag shows, choreography and dance music spanning house, pop and techno form its programme.

changes.name: Company Club
changes.before: Company Roma is the ultimate, unapologetic honey pot for Rome's bear community and their hot admirers. Following the massive footprint of its legendary sister bar in Milan, this subterranean den has cemented itself as a foundational pillar of Eternal City nightlife. It’s a beautifully raw, attitude-free sanctuary that seamlessly mixes cozy, high-energy retro social spaces with a naughty underground edge. From booming drag bingo and hilarious karaoke showdowns to sweaty, late-night floor-fillers dropped by guest circuit DJs, Company serves pure, unfiltered body positivity and local brotherhood.
changes.after: Company Roma is a basement bar connected to the bear community and admirers. Social drinking, drag bingo, karaoke and guest-DJ nights make up its programme.

changes.name: LeccoMilano
changes.before: Welcome to the undisputed social engine of the gay district! LeccoMilano is giving "urban garden realness meets high-fidelity social hub." Located on the iconic Via Lecco, this spot is a "safe and vibrant" sanctuary that transitions seamlessly from a sunny afternoon aperitivo spot to a high-energy pre-club powerhouse. The vibe is vibrant, inclusive, and effortlessly cool, featuring a sleek, industrial-chic interior and a sprawling sidewalk patio that is the ultimate stage for seeing and being seen. It’s the "living room" of Porta Venezia where the lighting is always warm and the welcome is even warmer.
changes.after: LeccoMilano is a bar on Via Lecco in Porta Venezia. An industrial-style interior and pavement patio accommodate afternoon aperitivo and busier pre-club evenings.

changes.name: Depot Milano
changes.before: Honey, strap on your harnesses because you are entering Italy’s absolute capital of raw, heavy-duty testosterone! Depot Milano is the largest, most unapologetic gay cruising and fetish mega-temple in Milan. Step inside a gritty, underground industrial blueprint that looks like a dark warehouse straight out of Berlin—where exposed bricks, black leather, and structural steel set the stage for pure, screen-free physical chemistry. It is a sex-positive fortress designed exclusively for the bold to sweat out their desires, strip down, and lose themselves to pounding electronic bass.
changes.after: Depot Milano is an adult gay cruising and fetish venue in Milan. Exposed brick, steel and a warehouse-style interior frame a setting focused on sex-positive adult events rather than a conventional cocktail bar.

changes.name: The George
changes.before: The George is the high-key sovereign of the Irish queer scene, having held court on South Great George's Street since 1985. As Ireland's oldest and most iconic LGBTQ+ venue, it serves pure "cultural institution" energy, acting as a rite of passage for young queer folks and a mandatory stop for international visitors. It’s a multi-level sanctuary where "Jurassic Park" (the cozy side bar for the older crowd) meets a massive, high-voltage dance floor that has hosted legends from RuPaul’s drag stars to Bananarama.
changes.after: The George is an LGBTQ+ bar and club on Dublin's South Great George's Street, established in 1985. It combines a smaller side bar with a larger dance floor and a programme of drag and guest performances.

changes.name: Cavo Paradiso
changes.before: Perched on a 150-foot cliff overlooking the Aegean Sea, Cavo Paradiso is giving "monumental open-air ritual". It is consistently ranked among the most impressive clubbing venues globally, designed to incorporate the island's natural beauty with its swimming pool and stone-carved dance floor. The vibe is transcendent, high-octane, and legendary—famous for the "Cavo magic" where you dance under the stars until the sun rises over the horizon. It’s a "bucket-list" sanctuary for any serious clubber, offering a high-fidelity sensory explosion of world-class sound, light, and breathtaking views.
changes.after: Cavo Paradiso is an open-air club on a cliff above the Aegean Sea in Mykonos. A swimming pool and stone dance floor are part of the layout, with DJ events extending into the early morning.

changes.name: Metropolis
changes.before: Metropolis Warszawa is Warsaw's sleek, multi-floor queer powerhouse where main-character pop-diva energy effortlessly collides with dark underground heat. Tucked right into the center of the capital, this spacious flagship sanctuary steps away from standard techno gatekeeping to deliver an massive celebration of pure, unadulterated nightlife freedom. The split-level layout divides your desires perfectly across two high-velocity dance floors: the Main Room serves up glittering, high-energy pop icons, remixes, and legendary local drag spectacles, while the moody Red Room cranks up the heavy tech-house and techno frequencies.
changes.after: Metropolis is a multi-floor queer club in central Warsaw. The Main Room focuses on pop, remixes and drag, while the Red Room offers tech house and techno.

changes.name: Ramona Bar
changes.before: Ramona Bar is Warsaw's deceptively large, mid-century retro lounge that serves major "pre-game cocktail playground" energy right in the beating center of the capital. Operating since 2013, this cozy dive hidden near the iconic Rotunda completely skips clinical minimalism to embrace warm, vintage wallpaper aesthetics, mismatched velvet chairs, and a highly welcoming, neighborhood-pub ambiance.
changes.after: Ramona Bar is a Warsaw lounge near the Rotunda, operating since 2013. Vintage wallpaper, velvet chairs and a mid-century interior create a pub-like setting for drinks before a later night out.

changes.name: XXL Club
changes.before: Get ready to submerge yourself into a legendary, multi-level powerhouse right on the absolute main artery of the Sitges Gay Village. For decades, Club XXL (famously known simply as XXL) reigned supreme as the village’s ultimate, uninhibited dancing and cruising fortress. In an absolute game-changing revamp, the legendary venue split its personality into a brilliant, high-octane double feature. Downstairs, the ground floor opens as the electric, neon-drenched GLOW Bar & Disco, packing a sweaty dancefloor with vocal house, heavy progressive beats, and high-energy pop anthems. But once you head up the staircase, you enter the infamous SHOWER ROOM—a sleek lounge bar hosting kinky weekend shower shows where the island’s finest performers get fully soaked under the neon rigs right in front of a buzzing, thirsty crowd.
changes.after: XXL in Sitges combines a ground-floor GLOW Bar & Disco with an upstairs lounge known as the Shower Room. House, pop and shower performances feature in its programme; check current listings for the night's format.

changes.name: El Horno
changes.before: Honey, if you are looking for the ultimate, long-standing cozy institution where the international bear and leather community drops anchor, march your paws straight into El Horno. Operating as an absolute village legend since 1984, this iconic taberna-style pub is famously known as the sister venue to XXL. Up front, it charms you with a warm, unpretentious rustic look and a bustling outdoor street patio that serves as prime real estate to watch the village strut past.
changes.after: El Horno is a taberna-style pub in Sitges with a connection to the bear and leather communities. A rustic interior and pavement seating offer a place for drinks in the gay village.

changes.name: Sitges Sauna
changes.before: Strip down, lock your gear away, and wrap yourself in a towel, because you have just reached the absolute, undisputed king of bathhouse relaxation on the coast! Sauna Sitges stands proudly as the first and only official gay sauna in Sitges. Located right in the town center, this two-story temple of flesh completely ditches stuffy commercial pretense for a spotless, deeply welcoming, and ultra-social atmosphere. Upstairs, it keeps things bright and modern with a busy lounge bar and a piping-hot wellness jacuzzi pool.
changes.after: Sauna Sitges is a gay sauna in the town centre, spread over two floors. The listing describes a lounge bar and jacuzzi alongside its bathing and adult social facilities.

changes.name: Raidd Bar
changes.before: Welcome to Paris’ most famous, splashy pop-spectacle. Raidd Bar is a high-octane, neon-drenched Marais institution that is unashamedly loud, proud, and campy. Split across a sleek street-level cocktail lounge and a buzzing subterranean dance floor, the venue is globally legendary for one specific thing: its nightly shower shows. Right on the main floor behind a massive sheet of glass, the bar features a fully operational, color-lit shower where jaw-dropping go-go dancers strip down and perform aquatic acrobatics. Backed by booming pop remixes, commercial house beats, and video screens, it is a high-energy, high-visual playground designed for absolute fun and sensory overload.
changes.after: Raidd Bar is a Le Marais bar with a street-level cocktail area and a downstairs dance floor. Shower performances behind glass are part of its entertainment programme, accompanied by pop remixes and commercial house.

changes.name: CUD Bar
changes.before: When the rest of the Marais district begins to turn off its neon signs and pack up the outdoor terraces, CUD Bar is just getting started. Operating as a legendary, double-decker after-party sanctuary, CUD is designed specifically for the night owls who simply refuse to let the sunrise stop them. At street level, the vibe is a calm, dimly lit, and hyper-social cocktail lounge perfect for casual conversation and people-watching. But if you descend the narrow stairs, you step straight into a sweaty, high-energy medieval vaulted stone cellar.
changes.after: CUD Bar is a late-night Le Marais venue arranged over two levels. A quieter street-level cocktail area leads downstairs to a dance floor in a vaulted stone cellar.

changes.name: Dalston Superstore
changes.before: The "Mecca" of East London QueerdomWelcome to the beating heart of Hackney’s queer scene! Dalston Superstore is an absolute powerhouse that serves as a kaleidoscopic playground—it’s equal parts thriving club, cabaret stage, laid-back café, and community art gallery. It’s giving "unapologetic East London edge" with its colorfully-painted doors, quirky sculptures, and industrial-chic vibes. Whether you’re there for a low-key coffee in the airy upstairs bar or losing your mind on the sweaty basement dancefloor, the energy is consistently electric and fiercely community-focused. It’s a "safe space" that prides itself on being a sanctuary for all-comers, from trans+ parties to cult-favorite drag brunches.
changes.after: Dalston Superstore combines a café-bar, cabaret programme, art displays and a basement dance floor in Hackney. Its queer-focused calendar includes trans-led parties and drag brunches alongside club nights.

changes.name: Fabric
changes.before: Descending into fabric feels like entering the mainframe of London's underground. This isn't just a club; it’s a sprawling Victorian meatpacking warehouse turned global techno cathedral. It’s giving unfiltered industrial grit—think raw brickwork, steel beams, and a multi-level maze of dancefloors where you can truly lose yourself. The vibe is music-first and hyper-protective, with a strict no-photo policy and a dedicated "Safer Spaces" team wearing "Don’t be a creep" tees. While it pulls a massive, diverse crowd, its soul belongs to the headsy ravers who come for the legendary vibrating "bodysonic" floors and stay for the marathon sets.
changes.after: Fabric occupies a former meatpacking warehouse in London, with exposed brick, steel beams and several dance floors. Its electronic music programme includes extended DJ sets. The listing notes a no-photography policy and a Safer Spaces team.

changes.name: Fold
changes.before: Welcome to London’s temple of the "unbound." Tucked away in an industrial estate in Canning Town, FOLD is giving raw, high-concept warehouse energy with a side of total liberation. This isn’t a glitter-and-pop fantasy; it’s a dark, smoke-filled sanctuary of industrial techno and electronic experimentation. The vibe is fiercely protective and inclusive, operating under a strict no-photos policy to ensure everyone can lose themselves in the music without the digital gaze. It’s an "extended session" powerhouse, famous for its marathon events like Unfold, where the party can roll for 24 hours straight in a haze of strobe lights and heavy bass
changes.after: FOLD is an electronic music club in an industrial estate in Canning Town. Techno and experimental programming, extended events such as Unfold, and a no-photography policy shape the venue.

changes.name: Vault 139
changes.before: Tucked away in the railway arches of Whitworth Street, Vault 139 is giving "underground secret" energy with a side of high-intensity play. This isn’t your shiny, corporate spa; it’s a raw, industrial-themed sanctuary that leans into its moody, dimly lit atmosphere. With its exposed brick walls and "no-frills" aesthetic, the vibe is unapologetically focused on connection and exploration. It’s a smaller, more intimate space compared to the city's mega-saunas, making it the perfect "insider spot" for those who prefer a darker, more intense cruising experience without the Soho glitter. (Pro Tip: Sundays are legendary here! They often host their most popular themed events, and the afternoon crowd is usually the busiest. It’s also worth checking their calendar for "Naked" or "Gear" specific sessions if you want to dial up the intensity!)
changes.after: Vault 139 is an adult cruising venue with a dim, industrial-style interior. The programme includes naked and gear-focused sessions; check the current event's clothing rules and opening times before going.

changes.name: Club Church
changes.before: Club Church is Amsterdam's most infamous, delightfully unholy house of worship where the dance floor meets the darkroom. Operating in the city center since 2008, this boundary-pushing cruise sanctuary ditches the stuffy pretense of mainstream clubbing and replaces it with pure, raw, body-positive hedonism. It's a split-level playground where high-energy house and techno tracks thump on the main floor while a labyrinth of cruising mazes, slings, and private cabins heat up on the balcony above. Whether hosting local drag royalty, trans pride gatherings, or intense fetish marathons, Church lets everyone unleash their wildest desires in a fiercely protected, sex-positive paradise.
changes.after: Club Church is an Amsterdam adult cruising club with a split-level layout. A main dance floor playing house and techno connects with cruising areas, slings and cabins. Themed events have different admission and clothing rules.

changes.name: De Trut
changes.before: De Trut is Amsterdam’s legendary, fiercely anti-commercial, collectivist Sunday night safe haven that has been sticking it to the mainstream since 1985. Tucked away in a former squatting complex in Oud-West, this non-profit, volunteer-run queer icon is famously known as a "dyke and faggot disco" that donates every single cent of its bar profits directly to global LGBTQIA+ activist projects via the Trut Fonds.
changes.after: De Trut is Amsterdam’s anti-commercial, collectivist Sunday night safe haven that has been sticking it to the mainstream since 1985. Tucked away in a former squatting complex in Oud-West, this non-profit, volunteer-run queer icon is known as a "dyke and faggot disco" that donates every single cent of its bar profits directly to global LGBTQIA+ activist projects via the Trut Fonds.

changes.name: Saarein
changes.before: Café Saarein is Amsterdam’s legendary, fiercely treasured feminist and queer matriarch. Nestled in the picturesque Jordaan neighborhood since 1978, a collective of ten women hijacked a traditional early 20th-century Dutch "brown bar" to create a radical, women-only safe space where flirting and organizing could happen without the straight male gaze. Today, it operates as a community-run foundation staffed entirely by volunteers. While it has lovingly thrown its doors open to all "queer-minded" people of all genders, it remains the undisputed, warm-hearted spiritual home for the city’s sapphic, lesbian, FLINTA, and non-binary communities.
changes.after: Café Saarein is Amsterdam’s treasured feminist and queer matriarch. While it has lovingly thrown its doors open to all "queer-minded" people of all genders, it remains the warm-hearted spiritual home for the city’s sapphic, lesbian, FLINTA, and non-binary communities.

changes.name: Nieuwezijds Sauna
changes.before: Gentlemen, welcome to Sauna Nieuwezijds (affectionately dubbed Sauna NZ), Amsterdam’s reigning premium gay bathhouse. Masterminded by the same creative, beautifully alternative geniuses behind the city's legendary Club Church, this place effortlessly ditches the tired, clinical vibe of ancient bathhouses for a sleek, modern, and high-design wellness look.
changes.after: Welcome to Sauna Nieuwezijds (affectionately dubbed Sauna NZ), Amsterdam’s reigning premium gay bathhouse. Masterminded by the same creative, alternative geniuses behind the city's Club Church, this place ditches the tired, clinical vibe of ancient bathhouses for a sleek, modern, and high-design wellness look.

changes.name: Club Panama
changes.before: Honey, let’s unpack the architectural glamour: Panama Amsterdam is not a full-time, dedicated gay venue, but rather a legendary mainstream megaclub that regularly throws its massive wooden doors wide open to host some of the most iconic, high-octane queer mass gatherings in Europe. Housed in a stunning, century-old industrial Port Authority warehouse right on the Eastern Docklands waterfront, this massive 1,000+ capacity theater-style fortress features towering ceilings and windows.

Housed in a stunning, century-old industrial Port Authority warehouse right on the Eastern Docklands waterfront, this massive 1,000+ capacity theater-style fortress features towering ceilings and windows.

changes.name: Radion
changes.before: RADION is Amsterdam’s brutalist, industrial cathedral of dance, where the walls are raw concrete and the energy is radically unrestrained. Housed in a repurposed former dental center in the city’s Nieuw-West district, this multi-room fortress operates on a coveted 24-hour license, making it holy ground for marathon techno purists. While it hosts premium electronic curation every weekend, RADION morphs into a fiercely sex-positive, queer-inclusive playground when it hands the keys over to legendary vanguard takeovers like Gegen Berlin, Pax-Romana, and Spielraum. Expect heavy bass, sweaty rooms, and an atmospheric, dark underground ethos that completely resets your nightlife expectations.

Housed in a repurposed former dental center in the city’s Nieuw-West district, this multi-room fortress operates on a coveted 24-hour license, making it holy ground for marathon techno purists. changes.name: Lellebel
changes.before: Lellebel (famously translating to "Jezebel") is Amsterdam’s rowdy, unapologetic, and spectacularly chaotic trans- and queer-womyn owned and operated stronghold. Throwing open its doors in 1997, this iconic jewel proudly brands itself as the only tiny alternative indie grunge rock queer bar in Amsterdam.

changes.name: Safari Disco
changes.before: Safari Disco Club is Barcelona's sprawling, wild, and high-energy jungle of unadulterated pop bliss. Part of the legendary Grupo Arena family, this massive two-room playground near Sants station sheds all electronic music elitism for a night of pure, sweaty euphoria. It’s the ultimate weekend pilgrimage for the city's diverse queer community, rotating through legendary themed nights. Fridays turn into the trash-pop and reggaeton heaven of Bananas Gay Party, Saturdays serve up the high-production house and vocal anthems of YASS! Barcelona, and select weekends play host to POPair, the absolute holy grail for bears and their friends looking to cut loose under a sea of neon.
changes.after: Safari Disco Club is a two-room Barcelona venue near Sants station, connected to Grupo Arena. Its rotating programme includes pop, reggaeton and house parties such as Bananas, YASS! and POPair. Check current listings for the format.

changes.name: Sauna Casanova
changes.before: Sauna Casanova is Barcelona's legendary, multi-level wellness playground built for pure, unadulterated exploration and absolute bodily freedom. Tucked right into the beating heart of Gaixample, this massive, high-production bathhouse effortlessly ditches moody, outdated vibes for a clean, sleek, and high-energy environment. Spread across sprawling subterranean zones, it seamlessly blends traditional wellness with adult nightlife. You can sweat it out in the massive Turkish bath, unwind in the bubbling jacuzzi, or navigate a sprawling labyrinth of cruise areas, private cabins, darkrooms, and mazes. It is a highly social, sensory-rich sanctuary where attitude is left at the door, and the freedom to connect, play, or relax is entirely yours.

changes.name: Apolo
changes.before: Sala Apolo is Europe's majestic, red-velvet grandfather of nightlife, wearing its 1940s theater bones like a badge of absolute indie pride. By day, this historic venue hosts cutting-edge underground gigs; by night, it sheds its skin to become a sweat-drenched, high-energy temple for sonic purists and free spirits. Spread across distinct rooms—including the grand, sweeping main hall and the dark, industrial electronic cave of La (2)—it pulls the cool, artsy, and alternative crowds of Barcelona. The undeniable holy grail for the queer family is "Churros con Chocolate", their legendary Sunday afternoon/night residency.

changes.name: Mango Bar
changes.before: Mango Bar is Vienna’s flashy, mirror-lined legacy hotspot that has been a vibrant rite of passage in the Naschmarkt queer district since dropping its anchor back in 1981. Wrapped in unapologetic, retro-pop neon aesthetics and wall-to-wall mirrors, this legendary basement joint operates on a fiercely welcoming "Labels are for drinks, not people" philosophy.
changes.after: Mango Bar is Vienna’s flashy, mirror-lined legacy hotspot that has been a vibrant rite of passage in the Naschmarkt queer district since dropping its anchor back in 1981. Wrapped in retro-pop neon aesthetics and wall-to-wall mirrors, this basement joint operates on a welcoming "Labels are known for drinks, not people" philosophy.

changes.name: Heaven Vienna
changes.before: HEAVEN Vienna is the glittering, historically monumental grand matriarch of the Austrian capital's queer clubbing history. Helmed for decades by the iconic, legendary drag pioneer Miss Candy (Holger Thor), this dazzling entity isn't just a party—it's a cultural movement that single-handedly evolved Vienna from a hidden "gay-only" underground scene into a sprawling, hyper-inclusive queer celebration. While it stepped out of regular weekly operations, HEAVEN commands a legendary legacy, periodically roaring back to life with spectacular, high-profile revival takeovers at monumental institutions like The Loft, Purple Club, and its original birthplace, the legendary U4 Club.

changes.name: Grelle Forelle
changes.before: Grelle Forelle is Vienna’s industrial, riverfront electronic titan that aggressively anchors the city's heavy underground subculture right on the edge of the Spittelauer Lände. While functioning as an uncompromising, international techno and house cathedral on standard weekends, this 1,000-square-meter concrete bunker is fiercely embraced as an LGBTQIA+ nightlife stronghold. It functions as the ultimate high-octane home base for legendary queer collectives like Club Meat Market and their explosive, dark-pop-infused FPlus* raves. Boasting a pristine, custom-engineered Pro Performance audio architecture that rattles your chest cavity, and a strict no-photography sticker policy at the door, it transforms into a smoky, dark, and beautifully liberated playground where you can sweat away your inhibitions completely out of sight.
changes.after: Grelle Forelle is Vienna’s industrial, riverfront electronic titan that aggressively anchors the city's heavy underground subculture right on the edge of the Spittelauer Lände. While functioning as an uncompromising, international techno and house cathedral on standard weekends, this 1,000-square-meter concrete bunker is embraced as a LGBTQIA+ nightlife stronghold. It functions as the home base for queer collectives like Club Meat Market and their explosive, dark-pop-infused FPlus* raves. Boasting a pristine, custom-engineered Pro Performance audio architecture that rattles your chest cavity and a strict no-photography sticker policy at the door, it transforms into a smoky, dark, and liberated playground where you can sweat away your inhibitions out of sight.

changes.name: Club U
changes.before: Club U is Vienna’s neon-soaked, underground retro jewel embedded right into the historic subterranean tunnels of Karlsplatz. Located directly beneath the iconic, Art Nouveau masterpiece of the Otto Wagner Pavilion, this intimate playground operates under the radical manifesto of being "schrill & schräg" (loud and eccentric). It features plush, curved black velvet seating areas surrounding a compact, high-intensity dancefloor. While daytime sees it function as a cozy café and sun-drenched terrace space named Karl & Otto, nightfall completely strips away its historic innocence.

Operating not as a permanent physical venue but as a massive, legendary monthly nomadic event brand, KEN bounces across Vienna's coolest underground fortresses—frequently packing out Camera Club, Das Werk, and Fluc. It splits its sonic personality perfectly down the middle, giving you a glittering main floor packed with high-tempo pop bangers, 90s trash anthems, and Lady Gaga loops, alongside a dark secondary room blasting heavy underground techno.

changes.name: Kaiserbründl Sauna
changes.before: Kaiserbründl Sauna is Vienna's ultimate imperial crown jewel of adult wellness, where palatial historic grandeur meets raw, decadent cruising culture. Housed inside a breathtaking 19th-century Neo-Renaissance palace that once served as a private bathhouse for Archduke Ludwig Viktor, this multi-floor institution feels like a living museum dripping in opulent frescoes, towering Roman columns, and vaulted architecture. It splits its massive layout into a stunning thermal sanctuary featuring a steam room, a dry Finnish sauna, a plunge pool, and a fully licensed bar lounge, alongside an intense, maze-like cruising floor complete with private cabins and darkrooms. It functions as a luxurious, historic escape where you can soak under imperial ceilings by afternoon and lose your inhibitions in a sprawling, multi-tiered labyrinth by night.
changes.after: Kaiserbründl is a gay sauna in a 19th-century Neo-Renaissance building in Vienna. Frescoes, columns and vaulted rooms surround a Finnish sauna, steam room, plunge pool, bar and separate cruising areas with cabins.

changes.name: Fluc
changes.before: FLUCC (traditionally known as Fluc) is Vienna's raw, architectural shapeshifter that stands as a gritty, haifischblau beacon of anti-commercial subculture right on the edge of Praterstern. Constructed out of an industrial stack of upcycled shipping containers and expanding down into a former subterranean pedestrian passage, this legendary twin-layered arts and communities hub operates on the radical manifesto of "Dance as Utopia". While serving as a massive hotbed for experimental indie-electronic music, underground techno, and live DIY performances, FLUCC is universally adored as a stanchly queer-inclusive, feminist-forward safe space.

changes.name: Chez Maman
changes.before: Chez Maman is Brussels' legendary, ultimate temple of pocket-sized camp and high-drama cabaret, serving up pure icon behavior since 1994. Tucked discreetly away down a cobblestone alley, you have to knock on the heavy closed door and face the discerning mood of the bouncer just to step inside this fabulous capsule. Once you make the cut, it is a gloriously intimate, packed, and high-energy time capsule where the main wooden bar counter literally doubles as the main stage. Led by Sugar Love and an elite cast of rotating drag royalty, the queens stomp, lip-sync, and sing in their own live voices directly over your cocktail glasses.
changes.after: Chez Maman is a small drag and cabaret bar in Brussels, where the wooden bar counter doubles as a stage. Performances include lip-sync and live singing. Space is limited and entry is managed at the door.

changes.name: La Reserve
changes.before: La Réserve is Brussels’ beautifully preserved, ultimate vintage treasure—proudly standing as the oldest operating gay bar in the city. Tucked seamlessly onto a cobblestone alley just steps away from the iconic Grand-Place, this intimate watering hole steps completely away from high-energy club lasers for pure, nostalgic tavern magic. Helmed by a wonderfully warm ownership duo (Sebastian and Benji), the Belle Époque-inspired interiors glow with stained-glass windows, dark wood paneling, and deep red velvet curtains.
changes.after: La Réserve is a traditional gay bar near the Grand Place. Stained glass, dark wood panelling and red curtains give the small room a Belle Époque-inspired setting.

changes.name: Homo Erectus
changes.before: L'Homo Erectus Bar (proudly curated by the adjacent fetish-haven Spit It Out) is a wonderfully quirky, kitschy, and kitsch-forward living room that stands as one of Brussels' absolute oldest and most cherished queer institutions. Channeling a wildly joyful design spirit heavily inspired by the vivid, eccentric aesthetic of filmmaker Pedro Almodóvar, this intimate den mixes 90s nostalgia with bold, unapologetic self-expression. It transitions seamlessly from a sun-drenched, quiet daytime terrace ideal for community chat into a bustling evening hub alive with pop-up events, Drag Race viewing parties, and friendly neighborhood banter. Run by the incredibly charming couple Tosh and Kriss, it provides a warm, authentic home-away-from-home where zero attitude meets excellent cocktails.
changes.after: L'Homo Erectus is a small queer bar with colourful decor influenced by Pedro Almodóvar's films. A daytime terrace gives way to evening events, including pop-ups and Drag Race screenings.

changes.name: Café Fontainas
changes.before: Café Le Fontainas is the ultimate bohemian, retro-chic neighborhood living room anchored right in the middle of Brussels' gay village. After briefly breaking hearts with a temporary closure, this legendary corner enclave has been beautifully resurrected by a collective of local creative minds to keep its iconic queer legacy thriving. It flawlessly bridges the gap between everyday coziness and festive open-mindedness—wearing all the colors of the rainbow while maintaining a punk-yet-fancy, hybrid vibe.
changes.after: Café Fontainas is a corner café in Brussels' gay quarter, with retro decor and a connection to the city's queer community. It combines everyday café use with a more social evening setting.

changes.name: Stammbar
changes.before: Stammbar is Brussels’ sleek, unapologetic capital of modern fetish and low-lit queer adventure. Situated right in the bustling veins of the Saint-Jacques gay village, this bi-level cruising juggernaut completely sheds traditional dive-bar dust for an immaculate, industrial-chic concrete setup. Up front, it plays the part of a trendy evening bar blasting raw electronic beats, house cuts, and progressive techno from world-class resident and international DJs. But push slightly deeper past the bar, and it descends into a high-temperature playground featuring a completely upgraded basement, locked-and-loaded darkrooms, and intense cruise zones. It’s a beautifully clean, highly charged sanctuary engineered for people to connect, shed their layers, and surrender to the night.
changes.after: Stammbar is a cruising bar in the Saint-Jacques quarter, with a concrete industrial interior. House and techno play in the social bar, with additional cruising areas and darkrooms on the lower level.

changes.name: Fuse
changes.before: Fuse Brussels is Belgium’s undisputed, longest-running techno institution, serving up pure sonic hypnotism since 1994. Housed in a raw, multi-level old cinema building in the Marolles district, this legendary industrial cavern skips commercial distractions for heavy, uncompromising sound systems and deep, immersive lighting. While it anchors Brussels' mainstream underground electronic movement with world-class techno residents, it holds a massive piece of queer heart: its legendary Sunday gay tea-dance nights are culturally famous across Europe. It is a dark, sweaty, and fiercely protective sanctuary designed entirely to let you dissolve into the BPM.
changes.after: Fuse is an electronic music club in a former cinema in the Marolles district. It has several levels, with techno at the centre of its programme. Check individual events for queer-focused parties and tea dances.

changes.name: The Agenda
changes.before: The Agenda is Brussels’ dazzling, modern crown jewel of queer nightlife, operating as the official, fiercely inclusive headquarters for the city's LGBTQIA+ and non-binary communities. Tucked into the lively Plattesteen corridor of the Saint-Jacques gay village, this ultra-chic, bi-level bar and club completely flips the script on the traditional "old school boozer." Fusing sleek industrial design with color-shifting neon light systems, it shifts effortlessly from a stylish evening cocktail den into a high-energy furnace of pure self-expression. From open-stage drag competitions, high-gloss viewing parties, and queer pop trivia to sweat-drenched weekend DJ sets blasting heavy house and pop bangers, it is a beautifully liberating safe haven where absolutely everyone is encouraged to write their own rules.
changes.after: The Agenda is a queer bar and club in the Saint-Jacques quarter's Plattesteen area. Its two-level interior hosts drag competitions, viewing parties, pop quizzes and weekend DJ sets with house and pop music.

changes.name: Heaven Club Prague
changes.before: Heaven Club Prague is the city’s sleek, ultra-modern subterranean playground that has been proudly setting the gold standard for Czech queer nightlife since dropping its anchor back in 1998. Tucked neatly into the lively Nové Město district, this dynamic, multi-tier wonderland cleverly splits its personality to satisfy every conceivable mood. Upstairs greets you with a bright, laid-back cocktail bar, a cozy chillout lounge, and a fully stocked on-site adult sex shop. But once you venture down the stairs, the atmosphere flips completely into a high-voltage, neon-drenched dreamscape.
changes.after: Heaven Club is a multi-level queer venue in Prague's Nové Město district. The upper area has a cocktail bar, lounge and adult shop, with a more club-oriented setting downstairs.

changes.name: Drake Club
changes.before: Drake’s Club Prague is the undisputed, non-stop grand patriarch of Prague's rawest adult playground scene, proudly holding the title as the city’s absolute oldest running gay cruising club. Tucked away on the other side of the Vltava River in Smíchov, this massive, multi-level fortress splits its personality into a tale of two eras. Street-level offers a cozy, dim-lit conversational bar lounge wrapped in neon accents and cheap pivo (beer). But follow the narrow stairs down and you unlock an enormous, medieval brick-winery cellar transformed into a hazy, labyrinthine cruising maze.

changes.name: Ankali
changes.before: Ankali is Prague’s moody, subterranean hypnotic maze that feels like a raw slice of Berlin nightlife transplanted directly into an old, repurposed soap factory. Tucked away in the industrial edges of the Vršovice district, this darkly curated techno bunker operates on a deeply emotional manifesto of being "happy and sad". While it is fundamentally a vanguard temple for abstract house, minimal synth, and industrial vinyl purists, Ankali is widely worshiped as a premier alternative queer safe space in Prague. Serving as the official canvas for legendary, sex-positive queer takeovers—like Pioneer Prague's infamous Hard DICK raves and the messy, slutty Homosteria and Aqueerius bimonthly jams—it features a strict no-photography sticker policy.

changes.name: Cross Club
changes.before: Cross Club is Prague’s sprawling, industrial cyberpunk labyrinth that looks like a living, breathing mechanical beast built entirely from scrap iron, cogs, and welded car parts. Tucked into the alternative Holešovice neighborhood, this legendary multi-floor, post-apocalyptic arts center operates on pure DIY ingenuity. While it anchors the city's mainstream-defying drum & bass, psytrance, and techno subcultures on a standard night, Cross Club is fiercely celebrated as a hyper-inclusive, LGBTQ+-friendly wonderland and transgender safe space.
changes.after: Cross Club is a multi-floor arts and music venue in Prague's Holešovice district. Scrap-metal sculptures, cogs and car parts shape its industrial interior. The programme includes drum and bass, psytrance and techno.

changes.name: Boudoir Bar
changes.before: Boudoir - U Sta rán (also fondly known to locals as Boudoir - U sta vran) is Prague's ultimate bohemian, candlelit hidey-hole that radiates pure, unadulterated artistic flair. Having recently migrated from its old Vršovice location to a fresh, intimate setup in Vinohrady, this delightfully eccentric sanctuary features cozy brick walls, mismatching wooden furniture, and strikingly bold, homoerotic artwork adorning the walls. It function as a highly welcoming, relaxed, and pocket-friendly neighborhood baseline where the gin selection is massive, the signature cocktails carry cheeky names like "Slut's Blood", and the vibe feels like drinking inside a progressive, artsy European living room.

changes.name: OMG Party
changes.before: OMG Party Prague is the undisputed, muscle-packed mega-circuit titan that completely dictates the tempo of Prague’s modern queer nightlife scene. Operating as a legendary, high-octane nomadic production team celebrating over 15 years of absolute dancefloor dominance, OMG is famous for launching the massive, official opening and closing night takeovers of Prague Pride weekend. When it drops its anchor into its ultimate industrial-chic home base, the multi-floor Mecca Club Prague, it throws open a portal of pure, adrenaline-pumping hedonism. Bathed in custom-designed laser grids, spectacular thematic visuals, and a chest-rattling Funktion-One sound system, the party unleashes a fierce matrix of international circuit house DJs, live vocal icons, and tantalizing international go-go spectacles. It is a sweaty, roaring, and completely uninhibited sanctuary where thousands of sexy circuit boys, club kids, and international tourists converge to kick off Prague's ultimate pride celebration.

Anchored by dual fast-service bars and an expansive main floor outfitted with neon-lit dance poles, it serves as an electrifying, high-voltage sanctuary.

changes.name: Centre Stage
changes.before: Think of it as the ultimate upgrade—retaining that intimate, "cosy" feel but leveling up with a passion for musical theater, pop bangers, and total inclusivity. It's where you go to serve main-character energy on the small stage, whether you're there for high-drama drag shows, musical bingo, or belting out your favorite anthems during karaoke.

changes.name: Oscar Bar
changes.before: Oscar Bar & Café is the stylish, sun-drenched sanctuary of Copenhagen's Rainbow Square (Regnbuepladsen). Right next to City Hall, this spot is a high-key community staple that manages to be a chic, inclusive cafe by day and a buzzing, beat-heavy lounge by night. It’s the ultimate "main character" venue where you can enjoy traditional Danish smørrebrød on the terrace or lose yourself to DJ sets on Friday nights. Best of all, it’s a non-smoking sanctuary, which is a rare and glorious breath of fresh air in the Copenhagen queer scene.

changes.name: Die Mumu
changes.before: Die Mumu is a Barbie-pink sanctuary in the heart of Cologne's vibrant Schaafenstraße gayborhood. This bar serves major "main character" energy with its glitter-drenched walls, swirling disco balls, and iconic lip-shaped urinals that are basically an Instagram requirement. It’s small, loud, and unapologetically fun—a place where you start with a cold Kölsch and end the night screaming-singing pop anthems with a high-energy crowd.

changes.name: Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld
changes.before: Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld (CBE) is an urban cultural powerhouse tucked directly into the historic railway arches of the Ehrenfeld S-Bahn station. This multi-space sanctuary—which often opens up into its sibling venue, YUCA—is a high-key favorite for the queer community. It’s the kind of creative hub where you can catch a soul concert in the evening and end up at an inclusive, high-energy party like the Chin Chin Party, House of Namus, or KISS. With three dance floors and a lush summer beer garden connecting the arches, CBE serves up pure "come as you are" energy for a diverse, multicultural crowd.
