changes.name: Bärenhöhle
changes.before: Bärenhöhle runs on that warm Berlin bear-bar chemistry where everyone clocks each other fast, then settles into real neighborhood momentum. It is less tourist showcase, more loyal local room with a playful, masculine-but-soft social tone that rewards staying longer than one drink.
changes.after: Bärenhöhle is a neighbourhood bear bar with a regular local crowd. The emphasis is on drinks and socialising rather than a large dance floor.

changes.name: Tabasco
changes.before: Tabasco carries old-Berlin gay-bar DNA: direct social contact, zero-frills confidence, and a room that has seen generations rotate through Nollendorf nightlife. The vibe is unapologetically classic and still delivers a useful late-stop social pulse.
changes.after: Tabasco is a traditional gay bar in Schöneberg's Nollendorfplatz area. It offers an informal setting for drinks and meeting other guests later in the evening.

changes.name: Der neue Oldtimer
changes.before: Der neue Oldtimer is classic Schöneberg continuity: camp touches, mature regulars, and that old-school Berlin comfort where everyone seems to already know the room. Less trend chase, more enduring neighborhood identity with strong regular-to-visitor crossover.
changes.after: Der neue Oldtimer is a traditional Schöneberg gay bar with camp decor and a largely mature regular crowd. It is a neighbourhood drinking spot rather than a dance club.

changes.name: SilverFuture
changes.before: SilverFuture brings Neukölln queer politics and nightlife into one room: mixed crowd, sharper social edge, and a community-first atmosphere that still turns fun and flirty fast. Great for travelers who want Berlin beyond rainbow-window dressing.
changes.after: SilverFuture is a Neukölln queer bar with a political and community focus. The listing describes a mixed crowd and an informal setting for drinks and conversation.

changes.name: Tipsy Bear
changes.before: Tipsy Bear is one of those joyful performance-driven spaces where drag, karaoke, and queer stage culture blend into nightly social electricity. It feels inclusive, playful, and intentionally loud in spirit without losing community warmth.
changes.after: Tipsy Bear is a performance-focused queer bar with drag, karaoke and other stage events. The programme shapes the evening, so check what is on before visiting.

changes.name: The Coven
changes.before: The Coven plays the premium cocktail card with queer intent: moody lighting, polished service, and a crowd that leans date-night-smart before drifting toward late-city spontaneity. Perfect for when you want Berlin nightlife to start with style, not noise.
changes.after: The Coven is a queer cocktail bar with low lighting and a more dressed-up evening atmosphere. It offers a smaller-scale alternative to a dance-club night.

changes.name: ILOsBAR
changes.before: ILOsBAR balances polished cocktails with real late-night Berlin movement: early social elegance, then a stronger dance-room pull on weekend hours. It works well as a bridge between Schöneberg bar-crawl mode and a more club-coded second chapter.
changes.after: ILOsBAR combines cocktails and social drinking with dancing during busier weekend hours. It can serve as an evening stop before heading elsewhere in Schöneberg.

changes.name: Zum schmutzigen Hobby
changes.before: Zum schmutzigen Hobby sits in the Revaler energy field where creative crowd, queer nightlife, and post-midnight unpredictability collide. Expect a rougher-cooler texture, stronger music identity, and a social vibe that feels very Berlin-now.
changes.after: Zum schmutzigen Hobby is a queer nightlife venue in the Revaler Straße area. Music and an informal creative setting are central to the listing.

changes.name: Capture
changes.before: Capture gives Friedrichshain queer nightlife a more art-forward lane: intimate room size, stylish but unpretentious crowd, and a social rhythm that is easy to enter even when you arrive solo. Great pre-club anchor if you want conversation before full dance-floor release.
changes.after: Capture is a small queer bar in Friedrichshain with an arts-oriented setting. Its compact room lends itself to conversation before a later club night.

changes.name: Betty F***
changes.before: Betty F*** feels like Berlin after dark compressed into one dense Mitte pressure point: fast entries, louder flirt energy, and a room that flips from cute to chaotic by weekend peak. Come ready for crowd heat, short eye-contact negotiations, and a very direct social tempo.
changes.after: Betty F*** is a small gay bar in Mitte. The room becomes busier and louder at weekend peaks, with drinks and socialising at the centre of the evening.

changes.name: Bears Amsterdam
changes.before: Get ready to hibernating in the best way possible, because Bears Amsterdam is the cozy, furry, and oh-so-friendly heart of the city's bear scene! This isn't just a bar; it’s a warm hug in the form of a neighborhood pub, where the "daddies," "cubs," and "otters" gather to serve authentic community realness. 🐻🇳🇱✨
changes.after: Bears Amsterdam is a neighbourhood pub focused on the city's bear community and admirers. It offers a small-scale setting for drinks and meeting other guests.

changes.name: Blend
changes.before: Get ready to double your pleasure, because Bar Blend is the glittering crown jewel of Amsterdam’s famous Reguliersdwarsstraat! This place is a two-story masterpiece of queer joy, where "elegance meets extra" and the cocktails are as stiff as the drag performances are fierce. 🍹👠✨
changes.after: Bar Blend is a two-storey gay bar on Amsterdam's Reguliersdwarsstraat. Cocktails and drag performances are part of its programme.

changes.name: Montmartre XL
changes.before: Sacrebleu! If you want to experience the legendary soul of Dutch queer history, Café Montmartre is your time-traveling ticket to 1980s glamour. This isn't just a bar; it’s a high-energy, sing-along sanctuary where the decor is "French boudoir" and the music is 100% pure, unadulterated pop and disco!
changes.after: Sacrebleu! If you want to experience the soul of Dutch queer history, Café Montmartre is your time-traveling ticket to 1980s glamour. This isn't just a bar; it’s a high-energy, sing-along sanctuary where the decor is "French boudoir" and the music is 100% pop and disco!

changes.name: Pamela
changes.before: BAR PAMELA is Amsterdam’s vibrant, uninhibited "queer living room" that has completely stolen the heart of Oud-West since dropping onto the scene in 2020. Founded by Dutch-Nigerian DJ and restaurateur Lola Edobor, this colorful corner sanctuary is fiercely dedicated to broadening the spectrum of diversity as a pivotal queer and BIPOC safe space. Pamela serves a little bit of absolutely everything sweet: meticulously crafted cocktails, rotating pop-up vegan fusion kitchens, weekly tarot card readings, drag spectacles, and steamy DJ dance sessions spinning anything from synth-heavy Italo disco to deep house and bass lines. It is a wildly welcoming home where regulars instantly become chosen family.

changes.name: Spijkerbar
changes.before: Lock up your bikes and let down your hair, because Spijkerbar is the absolute OG of Amsterdam’s queer nightlife! 🛠️🌈 Since 1979, this legendary spot in the Kerkstraat has been serving up "neighborhood pub" vibes with a side of "wildest night of your life." It’s unpretentious, high-energy, and a total safe haven for everyone from leather daddies to local legends.
changes.after: Spijkerbar is a gay neighbourhood bar on Kerkstraat in Amsterdam, established in 1979. It has connections to the local leather community as well as a broader regular crowd.

changes.name: Taboo
changes.before: Get your fans ready to clack, because Taboo Bar is the beating heart of Amsterdam’s "pinkest" street, the Reguliersdwarsstraat! This isn't just a bar; it’s a high-energy, neon-soaked stage where "Main Character Energy" is the only requirement for entry. Whether you’re here for a social afternoon tipple or a midnight lip-sync battle, Taboo serves it all with a side of extra. 🍹👠✨
changes.after: Taboo Bar is on Amsterdam's Reguliersdwarsstraat, combining afternoon drinks with a louder evening setting. Pop music and lip-sync performances are among the activities described in the listing.

changes.name: The Queen's Head
changes.before: Step into the royalty you are, because The Queen’s Head is one of Amsterdam’s most iconic and longest-standing queer jewels! 👑✨ Perched right on the edge of the historic Red Light District, this place perfectly blends "old-school Dutch cozy" with "high-glam drag fantasy." Whether you want a quiet beer by the canal or a wild night of bingo, the Queen is ready to receive you!
changes.after: The Queen's Head is a canal-side queer bar near Amsterdam's Red Light District. Its programme includes drag and bingo alongside quieter times for a drink.

changes.name: Fiesta y Bar Jolie
changes.before: Get your glitter ready, because Fiesta Jolie (and its home base, Bar Jolie) is the beating heart of queer culture in Buenos Aires! 🏳️‍🌈✨ Located in the trendy Palermo neighborhood, this isn't just a bar or a party; it’s a rite of passage. It’s the place where freedom is served in a glass, pop is a religion, and dancing until dawn is the only way to go.
changes.after: Fiesta Jolie combines a bar and queer party programme in Buenos Aires' Palermo neighbourhood. Pop music and late-night dancing are central to the format.

changes.name: Fiesta Puerca
changes.before:
Hold onto your hats, darling, because Fiesta Puerca is the wild, messy, and absolutely legendary younger sibling of the Buenos Aires queer scene! 🐷✨ Hosted at the massive Teatro Vorterix, this party is where you go to lose your inhibitions and find a dance floor packed with the city's most energetic youth. If Fiesta Plop is the campy queen, Puerca is the rebellious party animal who stays out until the sun comes up.
Queer Community Tips:  Wild Theme Realness: Every party has a different, often unhinged theme—think "sexy McDonald's employees" or "unexpected ambulance rides". Check their socials to see if you need to serve a specific look! 🎭Pop & Cumbia Mashup: Get ready for a high-energy mix of International Pop, Reggaeton, and Cumbia. It’s the kind of music that makes you forget your name and remember every lyric.Young & Restless: It hosts one of the youngest gay crowds in the city. changes.name: El Cangrejo
changes.before:
El Cangrejo is Barcelona's beloved, glittering, and unapologetically retro drag-pop time capsule. While it historically built its iconic, legendary name as a wild underground sanctuary in the gritty winding streets of El Raval (a kitschy tavern loaded with Spanish hits, cabaret theatrics, and neighborhood vibes), the brand has also established a fantastic second outpost, El Cangrejo Eixample, directly inside the city's main queer district. Step into either spot and you are instantly enveloped in a sweat-drenched, high-camp paradise where standard club elitism goes to die. Expect zero attitude, a booming dance floor bouncing to trashy 70s, 80s, 90s hits and Spanish pop anthems, and spectacular, laugh-out-loud drag shows that turn the entire crowd into a unified chorus.
Obs: Eixample Location: Carrer de Villarroel, 88, L'Eixample, 08011 Barcelona, Spain.

changes.before: If you are looking to wrap yourself in pure, otherworldly opulence while sipping something smoky, slide into a velvet booth at Harringtons Cocktail Lounge. Located upstairs in the buzzing East City district, this boutique lounge serves vintage 1920s glamour mixed with modern-day swagger. With massive panoramic windows overlooking the street, beautifully polished dark wood accents, and lush greenery dripping from the ceiling, it feels like a secret velvet sanctuary for the city's sophisticated tastemakers. By day, it’s a candlelit, upscale dinner spot famous for its legendary wine-pairing and whiskey supper clubs. But honey, don't let the white-linen dinners fool you—as the clock ticks closer to midnight, the tables vanish, local house and disco DJs take over the boutique booth, and the room transforms into a sleek, high-energy dance parlor where Cape Town’s chicest queer professionals and creatives come to get loose.

changes.name: Gat Party
changes.before: Dust off your boots, grab your favorite partner, and get ready for a completely unique spin on queer nightlife. Gat Party is Cape Town's legendary, high-energy monthly social that flips traditional Afrikaans ballroom culture right on its head. Forget stiff, judgmental club scenes; this is a beautifully camp, joyful, and completely unpretentious jol where the LGBTQIA+ family and their allies gather to spin across the floor. Serving pure nostalgia with a side of modern flair, the speakers blast a mix of classic langarm-sokkie, line-dance bops, 80s throwbacks, and country hits. It operates on a strictly "Bring Your Own" (BYO) basis, giving it a cozy, community-driven community hall picnic vibe where the laughs roll as easily as the dance steps.

changes.name: GBar Liverpool
changes.before: Welcome to Liverpool’s most infamous, longest-running after-hours temple of electronic sin. Operating for nearly three decades on Eberle Street, GBar Liverpool is an absolute institution that essentially dictates how the city's Gay Quarter behaves when the sun goes down. This sprawling multi-room labyrinth ditches standard commercial pop for underground, sweaty, pulse-pounding rave architecture across three distinct zones. Ground level features The Church—a stunning room hosting legendary resident drag queens blasting vocal house and kitchen disco classics. Move into The Boosh for deep commercial rhythms and R&B, before descending into the undisputed crown jewel: The BASSment. A dark, concrete bunker rigged with custom Void sound systems, it blasts fierce techno and tech-house until 8:00 AM. It is chaotic, euphoric, and a mandatory rite of passage for global music lovers.

Dressed in dramatic pink neon lighting, plush leopard print, and sparkling mirror walls, this basement sanctuary discards elite club pretension in favor of entertainment. It is loud, and social. Host to some of the sharpest, most hilariously savage drag queens in the North West of England, the tiny stage here is a non-stop rotation of live cabaret, chaotic karaoke show-downs, and lip-sync battles. It functions as the neighborhood's party starter, where the cocktails are heavily poured, the pop anthems are belted out by the entire room and the energy feels like a giant, chaotic hen party where everyone is invited.

changes.name: The Masquerade
changes.before: Welcome to the undisputed home of Scouse hospitality and zero-attitude neighborhood warmth. Known affectionately across the city simply as "The Mazzie", The Masquerade Bar proudly wears its crown as "Liverpool’s Friendliest Gay Bar". Tucked down a cozy city center street in the heart of the Pride Quarter, this legendary stalwart has been a community anchor for over 30 years. It drops all elite, high-gloss pretension at the door in favor of cozy, traditional pub aesthetics elevated by campy neon lights and a brilliant sound system.

changes.name: The Lisbon
changes.before: Welcome to the absolute architectural masterpiece of Liverpool’s queer heritage. Housed inside a stunning, Grade II listed Victorian basement dating back to 1903, The Lisbon Bar is a true legendary matrix of the Pride Quarter. Walking down its iconic wood-paneled stairs reveals a breathtaking subterranean palace featuring a magnificent, ornate plaster-work ceiling, cozy leather booth alcoves, and a sweeping, historic island bar counter. It completely bypasses elite club posturing in favor of a warm, traditional British pub feel fused with high-camp entertainment. By day, it serves as a relaxed, bright neighborhood sanctuary to grab a traditional pub meal or a pint. But when darkness falls, the ambient lights drop into a warm glow, the music swells, and the room transforms into a boisterous arena of chaotic karaoke nights, live drag cabaret shows, and hands-in-the-air pop singalongs that keep the room buzzing with laughter.

changes.name: Stock Bar
changes.before:
A legendary pillar of Montreal's Gay Village nightlife since 1996. Stock Bar Montréal is North America’s premier full-nude male strip club, celebrated for its high-energy atmosphere, athletic showmanship, and premium adult entertainment. Located right in the heart of the action on Sainte-Catherine Street, this sleek venue features an alternating roster of over 60 of the most muscular jocks and hunks delivering top-tier solo, duo, and famous shower performances.
✨ The Vibe: 
Athletic Eroticism: High-octane routines that blur the lines between feats of strength, choreography, and pure tease.Inclusive & High-Energy: Welcomes a lively, diverse, and respectful crowd of international travelers, groups, and locals. Action-Packed Weekends: Fridays and Saturdays feature dynamic multi-dancer routines on stage, alongside intimate private dance options.Modern Tech Edge: Famous for being a pioneer in streaming its nightly live stage performances globally for online members.
changes.after: Stock Bar is a male strip club on Sainte-Catherine Street in Montreal's Village, established in 1996. The programme includes solo and group stage performances, shower shows and private dances. The venue also streams some performances online.

changes.name: Le Belmont
changes.before:
A shape-shifting icon of Montreal nightlife for over 35 years. Le Belmont is a legendary, multi-functional nightclub and live concert venue located in the trendy Plateau-Mont-Royal district. Known for its intimate 350-capacity room, three bars, and a chameleon-like identity, this space fluidly morphs night after night—hosting everything from raw indie rock gigs and hip-hop hubs to sweaty underground electronic parties, reggaeton nights, and burlesque shows.
✨ The Vibe:
Eclectic & Mutant-Hybrid: Refusing to lock itself into a single music genre, the venue acts as a creative canvas for diverse local promoters, indie bands, and global DJs. Intimate Intoxication: A compact, high-energy layout that features a pulsing dancefloor right in front of the performance stage, ensuring a sweaty, high-connection clubbing experience.  Chic Yet Gritty: Blends a historic, neighborhood-landmark aura with cutting-edge visual production and an "Instagrammable" aesthetic that attracts a stylish, music-first crowd.Summer Extension: Features a vibrant terrace setup often utilized for open-air afternoon block parties and sun-drenched pre-club sets.
changes.after: Le Belmont is a concert venue and nightclub in Plateau-Mont-Royal. Its room and three bars host indie concerts, hip-hop, electronic parties, reggaeton and burlesque, with a terrace used for some summer events.

changes.name: Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth
changes.before:
A luxurious, historic icon with a deeply inclusive soul. Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth is one of Montreal’s most celebrated luxury hotels, world-famous as the site of John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s 1969 "Bed-In for Peace." Beyond its rich history, this grand property is proudly TAG Approved (the global gold standard for LGBTQ+ welcoming hotels) and an official partner of Fierté Montréal (Montreal Pride). It perfectly blends old-world elegance with a progressive, welcoming environment right in the heart of downtown.
🏋️‍♂️ Amenities: Indoor pool, state-of-the-art wellness center, luxury spa (Moment Spa), and a sprawling urban market (Marché Artisans).
changes.after: Fairmont The Queen Elizabeth is a downtown Montreal hotel associated with John Lennon and Yoko Ono's 1969 Bed-In for Peace. Facilities include an indoor pool, wellness centre, spa and the Marché Artisans food market.

changes.name: Kavros Beach
changes.before: Kavros Beach (often referred to alongside Peristeras Beach) is a sprawling, sun-drenched sandy dreamscape that pulls off a flawless double life on Crete’s northern coastline. While the mainstream resort strips nearby cater heavily to typical vacationers, taking a short stroll down the coast reveals an absolute heavenly oasis for gay sunbathers and naturists. Framed by gentle, sweeping sand dunes and wild coastal thickets, it drops any uptight commercial rules. This is a beautifully laid-back, open-air slice of paradise where clothes are entirely optional, the Aegean sea is crystal clear, and the localized dunes serve as a discreet, high-vibe cruising network for travelers and locals alike

changes.name: Apollo Party Crete
changes.before: Apollo Party Crete is the undisputed crown jewel and historical pioneer of dedicated, community-led queer nightlife takeovers on the island of Crete. Born out of a radical necessity to create spaces for the community outside of mainland Athens, this nomadic mega-event operates as a glittering, high-energy traveling circus. It packs out some of Chania’s best club footprints (like Da Vinci or Garage) and turns them into full-throttle temples of pride. The atmosphere is a spectacular, campy cocktail of world-class Athens drag legends, pulsing electronic-pop mashups, and raw, theatrical crowd interaction where the whole room becomes one giant, sweat-soaked family.
changes.after: Apollo Party Crete is a travelling queer party rather than a fixed venue. Events in Chania combine drag performances with electronic and pop music. Check each listing for the host venue and date.

It feels less like a traditional lounge and more like a glamorous, heavily curated attic owned by an eccentric, globe-trotting queer aunt. The entire space is packed wall-to-wall with velvet drapes, antique mirrors, glowing vintage lamps, and a gloriously chaotic array of retro artifacts that command your attention. Even the restroom is legendary for its bizarrely theatrical, over-the-top design. It is inherently camp, wonderfully poetic, and functions as a deeply comforting sanctuary for intellectuals, dreamers, and anyone looking to sink into a warm, candlelit haze with a finely crafted cocktail.

changes.before:

Nestled in the pulsing veins of the trendy Blloku district, this legendary establishment isn't a dedicated gay bar—as Albania’s capital lacks permanent brick-and-mortar queer clubs—but it is universally celebrated as the most open-minded, fiercely LGBTQ+ friendly and alternative sanctuary in town.

The interior is a beautifully curated, colorful museum of Balkan nostalgia—packed with dozens of vintage glowing radios, retro typewriters, mid-century furniture, and cinematic pop-art posters. Grab one of their world-class signature cocktails, like the Balkan Collins featuring local raki, and move out to their massive, plant-fringed courtyard terrace.

Step inside, and you are enveloped in a striking, eclectic Middle Eastern and Asian-inspired interior draped with moody lighting, low chairs, and intricate Buddhist artifacts.

changes.name: Bar Le Stud
changes.before:
Bar Le Stud is Montreal's legendary, unapologetic epicenter for the hairy, leather-clad, and body-positive corner of the Gay Village. Holding it down since 1995, this authentic staple celebrates its 30th anniversary as the city’s premier sanctuary for daddies, bears, cubs, and the leather/fetish community.
🐻 The Vibe: Thick, dark, and wonderfully testosterone-heavy. Le Stud is a massive, multi-level maze of pure masculine camaraderie where body hair is celebrated and pretense is left at the door. Downstairs features classic pool tables and a chilled-out dive bar aura perfect for cheap daytime beer specials and chatting. Upstairs transforms on the weekends into a sweaty, high-energy disco dance floor pumping out fierce club beats. It is the proud official home for BLUF (Breeches Leather Uniform Fanatics) meetups, host to rowdy Sunday Tea Dances, and legendary for its unhinged Monday and Tuesday night VOX karaoke. There is also a back patio courtyard for catching a breeze between drinks.
changes.after: Bar Le Stud is a Montreal Village bar with ties to the bear, leather and fetish communities. It combines pool tables and daytime drinks downstairs with weekend dancing upstairs, plus a courtyard patio. The programme includes karaoke and themed gatherings.

changes.name: Le Date Karaoke
changes.before:
Le Date Karaoke is the crown jewel of the Gay Village where karaoke isn't just a casual bar gimmick—it is a full-blown competitive sport and a campy rite of passage. If you have ever wanted to belt out Céline Dion or disco anthems in front of the most supportive, beautifully chaotic queer crowd in Montreal, this is your stage.
🎤 The VibeHigh-key main character energy. Le Date is an iconic, friendly piano-and-karaoke bar that has been anchoring Sainte-Catherine Est with pure joy and zero pretense. The room boasts a professional sound system, a music vault loaded with over 70,000 tracks, and slick stage lighting that makes everyone look like a superstar. What truly sets it apart is its unique, tech-forward flex: it is the only karaoke bar in North America that records your performance in high-definition MP4 video. You can download your set right to your phone to prove to your group chat that you absolutely crushed it. Grab a pitcher of sangria, cheer on the local drag icons, and prepare for a room full of strangers to turn into your ultimate hype team.
changes.after: Le Date is a karaoke and piano bar on Sainte-Catherine Est in Montreal's Village. It has stage lighting, a large song catalogue and a system for recording performances. Check with the venue about how recordings are shared or downloaded.

changes.name: Le Weiser
changes.before:
Le Weiser is Montreal's hot new addition to the Gay Village, proving that you can absolutely track sports brackets while remaining fiercely, unapologetically queer. Opened as an inclusive sports pub, this spot bridges the gap between high-stakes game days and ultimate community comfort.
⚽ The Vibe: Sporty, high-energy, and beautifully inclusive. Ditch the toxic masculinity of traditional sports bars; Le Weiser is a certified transgender safespace and LGBTQ+ haven. The space features a massive lineup of 17 screens showing up to 4 different games simultaneously—meaning you can catch Montreal Canadiens hockey, the FIFA World Cup, or major tennis tournaments alongside an incredibly diverse crowd. When your eyes aren't glued to the screen, they serve up free popcorn, retro arcade games, pool tables, and even a terrace equipped with mini-golf. They also host chaotic, campy watch parties featuring local drag royalty like Moh Dafok to commentate the matches.
changes.after: Le Weiser is a sports pub in Montreal's Village, showing several games across multiple screens. Pool, arcade games and a terrace with mini-golf add other activities, and some match screenings include drag hosts.

changes.name: Motel Motel
changes.before:
Motel Motel is the ultra-sleek, fluid hidden nightclub in the heart of the Gay Village. Masterminded by the creative team behind the legendary neighbor Bar Renard, this seductive venue is designed entirely for late-night connection, deep beats, and free spirits.
🪩 The Vibe: Discreet, hypnotic, and double-sided. From the street, it looks like a chic, well-behaved little bar perfect for a cozy cocktail warm-up. But once you step past the heavy velvet curtain, the real magic happens: you are pulled into an intimate, neon-drenched dreamscape thick with fog and shifting lights. The venue has a razor-sharp musical identity, packing the dance floor with local and guest DJs spinning raw tech house, deep house, and hypnotic minimal techno. It is a flawless mix of cozy lounge intimacy and underground club energy where the Village's alternative crowd comes to lose themselves until dawn.
changes.after: Motel Motel is a bar and nightclub in Montreal's Village from the team behind Bar Renard. A front cocktail area leads through a curtain to a smaller dance floor, with local and guest DJs playing tech house, deep house and minimal techno.

changes.name: Maison Des Jardins
changes.before:
Maison Des Jardins is Montreal's premier queer-owned oasis, redefining the classic bed-and-breakfast experience right in the beating heart of the Gay Village. Run by a genuinely warm-hearted local team, this 4-star destination is the ultimate cozy hideaway for travelers wanting true community comfort.
Elegant, peaceful, and fiercely LGBTQ+ friendly. Tucked away on a quiet street just moments from the roaring nightlife of Sainte-Catherine, this charming boutique inn strikes a perfect balance between homey comfort and vacation luxury. The interior boasts uniquely designed, spacious rooms (with options for private or budget-friendly shared baths). The absolute crown jewel is the beautiful, lush backyard garden oasis—complete with an outdoor hot tub and a stunning sun terrace where you can detox from the night before. To top it all off, the divine, freshly baked hot breakfasts are served community-style every morning, giving you the perfect chance to swap stories with global queer travelers.
changes.after: Maison Des Jardins is a queer-owned bed and breakfast in Montreal's Village. Rooms have private or shared bathrooms, and the property includes a garden, outdoor hot tub and sun terrace. Breakfast is served communally.

changes.name: La Loggia Art B&B
changes.before: La Loggia Art B&B is Montreal’s ultimate art-infused, queer-created urban sanctuary right in the heart of the Gay Village. Founded by partners Rob and Joel, this unique 3-star bed and breakfast flawlessly blends a boutique travel stay with personal growth, local art distribution, and creative workshops.

Founded by partners Rob and Joel, this unique 3-star bed and breakfast blends a boutique travel stay with personal growth, local art distribution, and creative workshops.

Housed in a beautifully restored 1867 building, this high-energy hotspot is globally famous for throwing global travelers and locals into one giant, beautiful mixing pot.

It is best known for its legendary weekly event programming—like its wildly popular, interactive "Ken Match" message-dating nights where patrons write notes to crush on strangers, and chaotic Sunday Superbingo drag shows hosted by icons like Coral Star.

With a tight, intimate 250-person capacity encased in premium acoustic design and deep blood-red lighting, it feels like a secret society for global heads. While it is fundamentally a polished, predominantly straight uptown space rather than a dedicated queer club, it operates as an LGBTQ-friendly haven that heavily attracts the city's ultra-chic, music-focused alternative crowd who gather to lose themselves in heavy, sophisticated sets of melodic techno, afro-house, and deep underground cuts.

While it functions as a highly respected bastion for underground minimal house, tech-house, and deep techno rather than a neighborhood queer bar, its high-art, zero-pretension crowd makes it an absolute LGTBIQ+ friendly sanctuary and transgender safe space.

changes.name: Federal Rooftop
changes.before: Federal Rooftop is Bogotá’s high-altitude, neon-soaked playground perched elegantly on the 5th floor above the city’s sizzling Zona T fashion and party district. Functioning as a hyper-trendy, beautifully fluid nightspot, it is a certified LGBTQ+ friendly and transgender-safespace where the city's cosmopolitan elite and global travelers unite.🌌 The Vibe:  Elevated, high-energy, and beautifully intense. Federal Rooftop masterfully blends sleek rooftop lounge luxury with raw, high-octane nightclub heat. The soundtrack here is a legendary, non-stop "crossover" cocktail—weaving flawlessly from sun-drenched house and Latin pop into sweaty reggaetón anthems and explosive global chart-toppers. Surrounded by panoramic mountain and city skyline views, a glittering disco ball, and signature flashing neon installations, the dance floor naturally stays packed. Come thirsty for premium signature cocktails, look out for their iconic theme nights like the touring BRESH party, dress to impress (no sportswear allowed), and get ready to rave under the Andean stars.
changes.after: Federal Rooftop is a fifth-floor bar and nightclub in Bogotá's Zona T, with views across the city and mountains. Its programme moves between house, Latin pop, reggaeton and chart music. Check individual events for clothing and entry requirements.

changes.name: Octava
changes.before:
Octava is Bogotá's globally ranked electronic mothership, consistently recognized by DJ Mag as one of the Top 100 Clubs in the world. Better known to locals simply as "La Nave" (The Spaceship), this 5-story powerhouse anchors the Chapinero district as a hyper-inclusive, transgender-safespace where house and techno purists dance strictly until dawn.
🪩 The Vibe: Immersive, futuristic, and fiercely high-fidelity. Stepping into Octava feels like boarding a sleek geometric starship dedicated to underground frequencies. The main floor boasts a modernist architectural design engineered specifically for flawless acoustic proofing, wrapped around a state-of-the-art sound system and high-res LED visual screens. Musically, they strike a flawless balance between championing local resident selectors and flying in world-tier titans—hosting everyone from Pan-Pot and Mauro Picotto to Afro-House legends like Maz. With its multi-level layout, fully furnished interior smoking lounge, stiff cocktails, and a beautifully diverse, phone-free focused crowd, it is the ultimate safe harbor to lose yourself in the bass.
changes.after: Octava is a multi-level electronic music club in Bogotá's Chapinero district, also known as La Nave. It focuses on house and techno, with local and international DJs, LED visuals and an indoor smoking lounge.

changes.name: Mad Radio Bogotá
changes.before:
Mad Radio Bogotá is the ultimate retro-futuristic audio sanctuary shaking up Bogotá's music scene. Serving as a hybrid online broadcasting booth, record boutique, and electronic nightspot, this queer-friendly and hyper-inclusive cultural center is where local vinyl collectors and alternative clubbers unite.
📻 The Vibe: Eclectic, artistic, and deeply music-centered. Mad Radio strips away the standard corporate club pretense to deliver a cozy, multi-environment space where "vintage meets urban". The venue splits its footprint across a breezy patio, a scenic terrace, and a pulsing indoor music hall equipped with an incredibly crisp, high-fidelity sound system. Musically, it is a boundaryless playground: you can walk in and catch a live daytime radio streaming talk, a groovy funk and disco warm-up set, or deep indie dance and raw underground house loops dropping after dark. The crowd is fluid, diverse, and fiercely dedicated to supporting independent underground selectors.
changes.after: Mad Radio Bogotá combines a radio booth, record shop and electronic music venue. A patio, terrace and indoor room host daytime broadcasts and DJ sets ranging from funk and disco to house and indie dance.

changes.name: Kinder Club
changes.before:
Kinder Club (formally known as Proyecto Kinder) is Bogotá's colossal, jaw-dropping electronic mega-club rewriting the rules of Latin American nightlife. Taking over a massive former historic school building in the heart of Chapinero, this structural marvel rose from the creative ashes of the legendary Kaputt Club to build a surreal, adult-sized electronic playground.
🪩 The Vibe: Berlin clubbing ethos meets a chaotic, playful dreamscape. Sprawling across multiple hyper-distinct micro-environments, rooms, and a massive outdoor courtyard, Kinder is so enormous that half the fun is literally getting lost inside it. The venue keeps things deliciously weird by pairing raw industrial techno, acid house, electro, and breaks with childhood subversions—think retro video games, quirky toys, and interactive art installations. It is an fiercely inclusive, LGBTQ+ friendly safe space and the proud playground for radical, queer, and body-positive electronic collectives like BULTO. From free vital water stations to top-tier international DJ bookings, this is an immersive, multi-sensory playground for the city's alternative alternative family.
changes.after: Kinder Club occupies a former school building in Bogotá's Chapinero district. Several rooms and a courtyard host electronic music events, with industrial interiors, retro games and art installations. The programme includes techno, acid house, electro and queer collectives.

changes.name: El Coq
changes.before:
El Coq is Bogotá's long-standing, beautifully eccentric nightlife jewel hidden away right in the city's upscale Zona Rosa. Serving as a proudly inclusive, LGBTQ+-friendly safe space, this legendary audio nest is where the city’s artsy, alternative over-30 crowd mixes with global party travelers over world-class selectors.
🐓 The Vibe: Vintage, sophisticated, and deliciously kitsch. Stepping into El Coq feels like entering a surreal fusion of a moody Spanish villa, a retro French country home, and a high-voltage indie disco. The interior is a sensory masterpiece, uniquely cluttered with old hanging photographs, vintage wallpaper, quirky household relics, glowing neon signage, and a legendary tree growing right through the center of the bar! Musically, it eschews aggressive, industrial techno warehouses for a hyper-grooved, soul-warming palette—expect global and local heavyweights spinning delicious sets of indie dance, psicodelic disco, deep house, and electronic funk reworks. It is an upscale yet entirely unpretentious oasis filled with beautiful, expressive people downing exceptional signature craft cocktails under blood-red lights.
changes.after: El Coq is a nightlife venue in Bogotá's Zona Rosa, with vintage wallpaper, old photographs, neon signs and a tree within the bar. Its music ranges from indie dance and disco to deep house and electronic funk.

changes.name: Capri Club
changes.before:
Capri Club is the self-proclaimed "owner of the chaos" (los dueños del desorden), reigning high above the bustling streets of Bogotá’s premium Zona T district. Operating as a beautifully chaotic, tropical rooftop sanctuary, this fiercely inclusive, queer-friendly hideaway is where the city's coolest crowd comes to misbehave and dance without rules.
🌴 The Vibe: Tropical, high-voltage, and deliciously uninhibited. Perched on the 3rd floor, Capri Club styles itself as an exotic, neon-soaked oasis right in the center of the city's concrete fashion matrix. The musical identity here is a wild, shape-shifting creature: midweek sessions focus heavily on electronic waves, bringing in the massive Solid Ground collective to spin deep afro-house, hypnotic minimal tech, and melodic tribal beats under the stars. Once the weekend hits, the script flips entirely into a sweaty, high-energy "crossover" and unapologetic reggaetón marathon. It is a stunning, beautifully diverse playground where top-tier local DJs keep the room pulsing, the signature craft cocktails flow heavy, and the crowd brings nothing but pure main-character energy to the floor.
changes.after: Capri Club is a third-floor rooftop venue in Bogotá's Zona T. Electronic music sessions feature during the week, with broader crossover and reggaeton programming at weekends. Check the current lineup for the night's format.

changes.name: Living 55
changes.before: Hotel Living 55 is a sleek, design-forward apartment-hotel hybrid nestled perfectly into the leafy, bohemian streets of the Chapinero neighborhood. Functioning as a hyper-modern residential sanctuary, this proudly LGBTQ+ friendly and inclusive destination is the ultimate cozy haven for travelers who want independence without sacrificing premium hospitality.
changes.after: Hotel Living 55 is a sleek, design-forward apartment-hotel hybrid nestled into the leafy, bohemian streets of the Chapinero neighborhood. changes.name: The Nudist Mansion
changes.before:
The Nudist Mansion is Bogotá’s ultimate, ground-breaking naturist urban sanctuary. Tucked away in a beautiful, character-filled house, this clothing-optional Bed & Breakfast is a proudly gay-owned, gender-neutral, and transgender-safespace. It was custom-built by hosts Fabián and Manuel to offer the global queer community a safe harbor of radical self-acceptance and authenticity without judgment.
🌸 The VibeL: iberated, comforting, and deeply authentic. Shifting away from standard hotel rooms, The Nudist Mansion encourages you to peel back the layers—literally—and shed your clothes along with any societal expectations. The interior features cozy, luxury private rooms equipped with hydromassage showers to wash away the travel stress. The heart of the home is a spacious shared living room complete with a roaring brick fireplace—absolutely vital for staying warm during chilly Bogotá nights. Guests can mingle naked with global travelers over complimentary morning coffee or fresh vegetarian breakfasts, or choose to relax in a hammock out on the lush interior and exterior terraces. Respect, body-positivity, and genuine human connection are the absolute laws of the house here.
changes.after: The Nudist Mansion is a gay-owned, clothing-optional bed and breakfast in Bogotá. Private rooms connect with shared living spaces, a fireplace and terraces. The listing describes hydromassage showers, morning coffee and vegetarian breakfasts.

changes.name: La Estación Café Chapinero

Housed inside a striking, century-old casona that is officially preserved as architectural heritage, this beloved café, restaurant, and lounge sits proudly just a few blocks away from the legendary Theatron mega-club.

changes.name: Spiaggia Il Buco
changes.before:
Spiaggia Il Buco (literally meaning “The Hole” beach) is Rome's premier, historically legendary open-air gay clothing-optional beach and cruising area. Hidden inside the protected, tranquil dunes of the Capocotta Nature Reserve roughly 30km south of the city center, it serves as the ultimate wild summer escape for Rome's LGBTQ+ community away from the straight tourist crowds. 
✨ The Vibe: Wild, remote, and highly liberated. The atmosphere here is deeply split between a relaxing, sun-drenched nude beach by day and a high-tension cruising ground by late afternoon. Because it is surrounded by rolling sand dunes and thick Mediterranean shrubbery, it offers total privacy. Most of the cruising action is concentrated just behind the beach towel area, woven directly into the sandy paths, dunes, and bushes. It attracts a mostly male, body-positive, and very open-minded crowd. Since it is located inside a nature reserve, facilities are non-existent directly on this stretch—giving it a rugged, untamed charm where you should definitely bring your own water and supplies.
changes.after: Spiaggia Il Buco is a clothing-optional beach in the Capocotta nature reserve south of Rome, with a history of gay cruising. The stretch has limited facilities, so bring water and supplies. It is a shared outdoor area; privacy should not be assumed.

changes.name: Limanakia Beach
changes.before:
Limanakia B is a legendary, rugged chain of coastal coves widely celebrated as the premier daytime gay summer hot spot in Athens. Located just 30 minutes outside the city center along the scenic Athens Riviera, this clothing-optional destination exchanges soft sand for dramatic rock cliffs and some of the most crystal-clear, glass-like turquoise waters in Greece.
✨ The Vibe: Wild, sun-drenched, and highly crusing-centric. The area is divided into three distinct rocky coves with varying levels of intensity. The first cove is a laid-back mix of nudists and clothed couples soak-bathing on the boulders. However, as you venture further east toward the third cove, the landscape transforms entirely into a heavily populated LGBTQI+ playground dominated by gay men. Because there is absolutely zero natural shade, guys spread out their towels on the flat limestone shelfs to tan before heading up into the surrounding brush, low trees, and rocky trails where the outdoor cruising action peaks. It is incredibly popular, body-positive, and packed with local Athenians and international travelers alike.
changes.after: Limanakia B is a rocky, clothing-optional coastal area on the Athens Riviera, with a long connection to gay beach culture. The coves have different mixes of visitors, and some surrounding paths are used for cruising. Shade is limited, so bring sun protection and water.

Restaurant Tendresse (fondly known as Bistro Tendresse) is the stunning plant-based darling located right in the vibrant beating heart of Montreal's Gay Village.
The Vibe: Honey, this is eco-chic elegance meets effortless neighborhood charm. It is visually gorgeous with sleek, minimalist decor and massive, sun-drenched windows perfect for checking out the local talent walking down Sainte-Catherine. It serves up a totally inclusive, open-minded environment where drag royalty, tourists, and gorgeous queer couples come together. It is the absolute premier spot in the Village for an elevated, guilt-free plant-based brunch date or sophisticated evening cocktails before you hit the dancefloors.

La Graine Brûlée (which cheekily translates to "The Burnt Seed") is an eclectic, hyper-colorful wonderland of a coffee shop sitting proudly in Montreal's Gay Village.
The Vibe: Honey, walk through these doors and you are stepping straight into a playful, maximalist circus. The aesthetic is pure, unapologetic kitsch with bright neon colors, arcade games, and whimsical amusement park touches. It is the ultimate queer community hub where local students tap away on laptops, creative minds gossip over matcha lattes, and everyone is dressed to impress. It is extremely Instagrammable, fiercely eco-conscious, and boasts a gorgeous summer street terrace that serves major people-watching realness. Come for the impeccable espresso, stay for the delicious vegan treats and the joyfully chaotic energy.

changes.name: Café Reine Garçon
changes.before:
Café Reine Garçon is a total dream—a fiercely queer-owned, ultra-inclusive neighborhood café, art space, and community sanctuary nestled safely in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal (bordering Mile End).
The Vibe: Honey, this is exactly where the neighborhood's artsy queer elites, non-binary creatives, and local poets gather to breathe. Founded as a literal safe space for emerging artists to showcase their talent, the aesthetic is peak cozy-indie: charmingly mismatched second-hand chairs, rotating local art prints on the walls, and a staff that treats everyone like family. It’s warm, deeply intentional, and zero-judgment. Come sit on their adorable little outdoor patio, sip a perfectly balanced specialty oat milk latte (their seasonal marshmallow or rose & vanille syrups are pure witchcraft), and bask in the gorgeous, calming transgender-friendly energy.

It’s trendy, wildly inclusive, serves a fierce transgender safe space, and packs a legendary daily happy hour to get your night started right.

RAUM’s philosophical identity treats queerness not as a static concept, but as an essence of constant movement and community resistance.The aesthetic inside is a masterclass in raw, immersive industrialism, heavily rooted in DIY ethics, innovative interior architecture and a world-class, ground-shaking sound system. The curation steers clear of generic pop-remix clubs; instead, it is an electronic purist's paradise, pulsating with hard-hitting techno, underground house, dark synth, and electroclash. The dance floors are incredibly energetic, intense, and deeply affectionate, populated by local club kids, avant-garde artists, and international audiophiles. To protect the vulnerability and freedom of the space, RAUM operates a strict door policy handled by community hosts—ensuring those who enter genuinely respect and uphold the safe-space culture inside. It is raw, authentic, and easily Amsterdam’s most exciting underground playground.

Rubber Parties. It is hot, intense, and deeply respectful, making it the definitive weekend destination for global fetish travelers.

Horoom Nights is a specialized, recurring LGBTQ+ party series engineered specifically to create a joyous, radical sanctuary of bodily and sexual freedom. changes.name: The Stranger Bar
changes.before:
The Stranger Bar (House of Drag Queens) is the ultimate crown jewel of Bangkok's drag scene and an absolute must-visit destination for your night out.
The Vibe: Honey, welcome to the epicenter of high-octane Thai drag realness. This isn't just a bar; it’s a living, breathing theater of queer joy where "strangers become family." Founded by the legendary drag queen M Stranger Fox, it delivers a flawless mix of fierce lip-sync battles, hilarious comedy, jaw-dropping choreography, and impeccable hosting. The space is loud, proud, cozy, and overflowing with electric energy. It balances the intimate charm of a neighborhood pub with the world-class talent of a top-tier stage production, drawing a beautiful, international crowd that is ready to scream, tip, and party.
changes.after: The Stranger Bar, also known as House of Drag Queens, is a Bangkok drag venue founded by M Stranger Fox. Lip-sync, comedy, choreography and hosting form the programme in a compact bar setting.

changes.name: Pride Bar & Circus
changes.before:
Pride Bar and Restaurant and its connected sister venue Circus Soi 4 are two powerhouse, side-by-side hotspots keeping the queer magic alive right in the center of Bangkok's gay district.
The Vibe: This double-feature is pure flamboyant theater mixed with an unpretentious neighborhood block party. Taking over the legendary spot that used to be Telephone Pub, Circus serves big-top extravaganza realness inside—think dramatic red drapes, sparkling chandeliers, glitzy drag stages, and high-energy pop/techno beats dropping courtesy of live DJs. Step onto the outdoor terrace shared with Pride Bar, and the vibe shifts into the ultimate chill, high-visibility runway. It’s the absolute best patio space on the street to grab a strong cocktail, enjoy some open-air socializing, and indulge in premium people-watching as the whole beautiful community struts past.

Stepping inside feels like walking onto an ultra-stylized, high-fashion movie set packed with curvy mid-century furniture, bold color blocks, and museum-worthy art pieces. changes.name: Nowadays
changes.before:
Nowadays is the holy grail of community-centric, open-air queer euphoria in New York.Where Basement is dark and industrial, Nowadays is bright, expansive, and soul-affirming. Operating as a massive indoor/outdoor gathering space on the Queens/Brooklyn border, it balances cozy living-room-style winter clubbing with legendary, sun-soaked summer marathons where the dance floor feels like a massive, diverse family reunion.
Practical Information & Inclusion:
The Space: A sprawling, tree-lined outdoor backyard packed with picnic tables and a venting dance floor, paired with an acoustically flawless indoor club room boasting a world-class analog sound system.
The Schedule: Famous for Nowadays Nonstop, a recurring 24-hour-plus weekend marathon party where ravers can dance through the night, eat breakfast on-site, and keep clubbing all through Sunday afternoon.
The Inclusion: It sets the global gold standard for safer nightlife spaces. Every night begins with a mandatory briefing on consent, and dedicated "safety monitors" roam the crowds to ensure everyone—especially trans, non-binary, and queer patrons—is completely safe and respected.

changes.before: Welcome to the uncompromising, radical powerhouse of Parisian queer feminism. La Mutinerie (The Mutiny) isn't just a place to grab a cheap pint—it is a fiercely political, fiercely self-managed anarcho-queer safe haven and cultural laboratory. Located right in the 3rd Arrondissement, this venue actively rejects mainstream, commercialized nightlife culture. It is unapologetically trans-feminist, deeply community-focused, and stands as a vital sanctuary for the counter-cultural margins of Paris.

changes.name: Sub Club
changes.before:
The low-ceilinged, sweat-dripping spiritual home of Scottish electronic music. Tucked away in a dark basement for nearly four decades, it holds the title of the world's longest-running underground dance club, powered by a legendary bodysonic dance floor that literally vibrates the music through your feet.

changes.name: HALL
changes.before:
The undisputed, cold-concrete Mecca of Baltic techno. Perched on the edge of the icy Baltic Sea in a former Soviet shipyard warehouse, it channels deep, unapologetic Berlin energy with a fiercely protective underground ethos that has completely revolutionized Estonia's nightlife scene.
Vibe: Raw, dark, and industrial. The main room features a bone-rattling Funktion-One sound system, blinding strobes, and heavy smoke, while the smaller Mesila room upstairs offers a more intimate, left-field experimental sonic experience.
Tips: Strict camera bans apply—the staff will tape your phone cameras upon entry. Respect the dance floor etiquette by keeping conversations off the floor; people are strictly there to dance. If you need a breather, step out to the rear deck to catch beautiful views of the Gulf of Tallinn.

When the original Storgata 26 tragically declared bankruptcy, the keys were handed over to create Labyrinth—a fresh, neon-lit, and bass-heavy underground multi-room sanctuary that has kept the building's iconic electronic legacy pulsing.
Vibe: Energetic, immersive, and visually stunning. The layout functions exactly like a maze: a dark, smoky basement blasting underground house and driving techno, an upstairs room flashing with funky 70s disco aesthetics and rainbow LED dancefloors, and a spacious backyard courtyard perfect for cool-air socializing.

changes.name: Lux Frágil
changes.before:
The undisputed, ultra-stylish crown jewel of Portuguese nightlife. Partially owned by Hollywood actor John Malkovich, this legendary waterfront club blends high-art design, breathtaking river-view balconies, and an absolute powerhouse sound system into a sophisticated yet beautifully unhinged queer-friendly paradise.
Vibe: A multi-tiered masterpiece of electronic music. The venue splits into three distinct floors: the ground floor basement (dark, foggy, raw, and pumping heavy underground techno/house), the middle floor (a highly stylized, pop, disco, and indie dance paradise with giant art installations), and the legendary Rooftop Terrace (providing unmatched views of the sunrise over the river).
Tips: Do not arrive before 1:30 AM unless you want to hang out in an empty room—the venue does not truly wake up until 2:30 AM.
changes.after: Lux Frágil is a Lisbon waterfront nightclub with several levels and river-view balconies. Electronic music, art installations and a rooftop terrace are part of the setting, with the programme varying across the rooms.

changes.name: Vent
changes.before: VENT Tokyo is a sleek, subterranean playground nestled right beneath the polished, high-fashion streets of Omotesando. It completely trades the flashy, commercial mega-club cheese for a minimalist, brutalist aesthetic that feels like a concrete modern art gallery dedicated entirely to the gods of underground dance music. With its strict no-photography policy on the dance floor, it creates a beautifully private, immersive sanctuary where you can sweat, move, and connect without a single phone screen ruining the atmosphere.

changes.name: Contact / Enter
changes.before: The legendary Tokyo club Contact sadly had to shut its doors permanently due to massive district urban redevelopment. However, its revolutionary spirit lives on through its direct successor, ENTER Shibuya. Opened by the exact same creative team, this intimate 150-capacity hot spot literally salvaged the pristine, airtight sound system from Contact's famous Studio X and bolted it right into this venue. The layout completely flips the script on traditional clubbing—the DJ booth is planted squarely in the dead center of the room. There is no stage and no barrier, dissolving the wall between the artist and a sweaty, hyper-focused dance floor.

changes.name: Phi Garden
changes.before:
Phi Garden is Tel Aviv's ultimate lush, open-air queer sanctuary hidden right in plain sight inside a stunning Bauhaus courtyard. It effortlessly executes a "triple threat" schedule: functioning as a relaxed daytime coffee hangout, morphing into a chic cocktail terrace at sunset, and finally exploding into a sweaty, high-energy electronic music haven when night falls. It is widely celebrated across the city's nightlife landscape for its unapologetic left-wing political stance. The venue functions heavily as a vital community engine, regularly hosting high-energy ballroom vogue functions, independent movie screenings, queer talk shows, and local activist gatherings.
Tips: Timing your entry is everything. They almost always offer a "Free Entry Until 00:00" rule for their standard club nights. Arrive precisely at 11:00 PM to skip the cover entirely. Order their signature local favorite, the ginger-kale-arak cocktail, to keep yourself hydrated and refreshed while dancing.

changes.name: Coda
changes.before: CODA Toronto is the undisputed heavy artillery of the city's electronic music nightlife. Born out of the team behind the legendary, defunct venue Footwork, this mid-sized multi-room hub completely rejects the hyper-glitzy, pretentious bottle-service cheese of Toronto's King West strip. Instead, CODA funnels its entire identity into raw, unfiltered dancefloor energy powered by a custom-engineered, heavy-duty Canadian PK Sound system that delivers bone-rattling bass straight to your chest. The layout features one massive, high-ceilinged main dancefloor draped under an iconic giant disco ball and deep minimal lighting, creating an intense, dark vortex where the city's real electronic music heads go to lose themselves entirely in house, techno, and underground bass.

changes.name: D-Edge
changes.before: D-Edge São Paulo is a world-renowned, architecturally mind-melting electronic cathedral that fundamentally transformed global club design. Conceived by owner Renato Ratier and designer Muti Randolph, this iconic multi-floor powerhouse in the Barra Funda neighborhood trades standard dark venue aesthetics for an immersive, futuristic cyber-grid. The entire main room is wrapped in an interactive system of over 200 linear meters of LED light strips that pulse, shift, and undulate in perfect synchronization with every kick drum and hi-hat. Boasting a razor-sharp, pristine sound system and a sleek rooftop terrace overlooking the dramatic São Paulo skyline, it feels less like a simple nightclub and more like stepping straight into the matrix or a high-end, cyberpunk sci-fi movie.

changes.name: Mamba Negra
changes.before:
Mamba Negra is not a standard brick-and-mortar nightclub; it is a legendary, independent nomadic queer collective that functions as the absolute vanguard of São Paulo’s radical underground rave scene. Founded by visionary women and LGBTQIA+ artists like Cashu and Laura Diaz, Mamba operates as an explicitly political act of reclaiming public and industrial city spaces. They nomadically take over brutalist abandoned factories (like the historic Fabriketa in Brás), open-air downtown squares, or raw studio warehouses, packing them with massive custom sound systems. Blending heavy, high-BPM industrial techno, dark acid house, and gritty Brazilian Baile Funk, it creates a wildly uninhibited, sweat-drenched sanctuary of absolute artistic, sonic, and sexual liberation.
Nomadic / Rotating location. They frequently activate historic industrial spaces like Fabriketa (Rua do Bucolismo, 81 - Brás, São Paulo), ZIG Studio (Av. Pacaembu, 33 - Barra Funda), or open-air street pop-ups right in the urban heart of Centro. Always check the event page for the exact coordinates dropped right before the party.

Tucked away in a dark, converted basement disco in the heart of the Central Business District, this boutique nocturnal playground brings a slice of uncompromising Berlin club culture straight to the Mother City. For over a decade, this raw, concrete dark box has single-handedly kept the torch lit for heavy, uncompromising techno, acid house, and drum & bass on the continent. changes.name: Gretas
changes.before: Honey, say hello to the reigning matriarch of Swedish nightlife: Gretas is officially Sweden’s oldest gay club! Holding down the fort since 1997, this multi-level crown jewel in the center of Gothenburg has been serving pure queer joy for nearly three decades. It is the ultimate unpretentious party house. Spanning two distinct floors, it masterfully transitions from campy Eurovision sing-alongs, retro '80s and '90s pop, and fierce drag performances on the main disco floor, into deep house, techno, and R&B up on the top deck.

changes.name: Park Lane
changes.before: Honey, if you are looking for a true Gothenburg institution that knows how to pull out all the stops, welcome to Park Lane. Sitting proudly at the very crown of the city's main Avenyn strip, this legendary multi-room megaclub has been welcoming a glorious mix of kings, queens, celebs, and party animals since 1991. While it operates as a glittering commercial krogshow (dinner theater) and high-energy mainstream dance palace on standard nights, its true queer soul ignites once a month. Park Lane is the proud, long-term host venue for Club Queer—Gothenburg’s flagship monthly gay mega-party that just celebrated 25 years of pure, unfiltered glitter, camp drag spectacles, and dance floor euphoria

changes.name: Hanlan’s Point Beach (Toronto Islands)
changes.before: Honey, welcome to the absolute birthplace of Canadian queer liberation: Hanlan’s Point Beach. Nestled on the western edge of the Toronto Islands, this legendary, southwest-facing stretch of pristine sand dunes is Canada's oldest surviving queer landmark. It famously hosted the nation’s very first Pride gathering (the "Gay Day Picnic") way back in 1971. Officially designated as a clothing-optional naturist haven, Hanlan's has been a sanctuary for gays to sun their buns in the buff since the 1940s.The specific cruising area—discreetly localized within the lush, winding trails of the bushes and sand dunes running parallel to the clothing-optional beach—operates with a deeply historical, laid-back, and social approach to connection. It is a world away from the fast-paced, high-pressure energy of downtown bathhouses or apps. Instead, it offers an organic, slow-burning playground where a shared glance on the ferry ride over blossoms into sun-drenched, natural chemistry hidden gently beneath the island foliage.

Housed in the legendary, sprawling framework of the historic Esquire Ballroom—the very stage where Patsy Cline crooned and a broke Willie Nelson scribbled the lyrics to "Crazy"—this 11,000-square-foot honky-tonk behemoth is the undisputed crown jewel of LGBTQ+ Country & Western culture in the South. Under a glittering pair of disco cowboy boots, you can glide across an expansive hardwood dance floor, knock back sweet frozen drinks across 10 bar stations, or shoot pool in the nostalgic Esquire Room.
changes.after: Neon Boots Dancehall & Saloon is a country-and-western venue in Houston's former Esquire Ballroom. A large wooden dance floor, several bar stations and pool tables serve its LGBTQ+ country-dance programme.

changes.name: Christopher St. Café
changes.before: Named in profound homage to New York City's iconic, liberation-sparking Christopher Street, this vibrant venue proudly stands as Mendoza's very first café structured entirely around LGBTIQ+ labor inclusion and community rights. Flaunting the rainbow pride flag colors directly across its storefront, it functions as an unpretentious, zero-labels sanctuary where patrons can "be themselves, without fear". It masterfully balances two worlds: operating as a cozy, laptop-friendly brunch hub by day before transitioning into an intimate, neon-tinted cocktail lounge and community art space by twilight.

changes.name: Six Colours
changes.before: . Celebrating nearly a quarter-century as a pillar of Granada's nightlife, this wildly popular bar skips moody underground pretense for pure, campy dance-floor euphoria. The interior is a delightful wonderland of eye-catching, eclectic decor, flashing light walls, and large video screens projecting a high-energy cocktail of Euro-pop, mainstream American and British club anthems, and timeless Spanish singalongs. It functions as a brilliant social crossroads; things start off chatty and laid-back early on, but quickly escalate into a beautifully chaotic, arms-in-the-air dance party as the clock strikes midnight.
changes.after: Six Colours is a Granada bar with eclectic decor, illuminated walls and music-video screens. Early evening drinks give way to dancing to Euro-pop, international club tracks and Spanish singalongs.

changes.name: Pub La Sal
changes.before: If you are looking to pay respect to the ultimate, foundational matriarchy of Granada’s queer nightlife, step directly into La Sal. Operating with pride since 1988, this legendary queer club originally opened its doors as one of the very first dedicated lesbian bars in Andalusia. Over nearly four decades, it has evolved into a beautifully inclusive, multi-generational safe haven where labels are discarded entirely at the entrance. The interior boasts a cozy, intimate, and dimly lit aesthetic where the dancefloor moves to a high-spirited mix of retro Spanish pop anthems, commercial hits, and throwbacks.

changes.name: Templo Spa Mendoza
changes.before: Operating as a sleek, highly modern oasis of male intimacy, Templo Spa Mendoza is the city's undisputed capital for physical relaxation and homo-socialization. It cuts through the digital fatigue of dating apps to offer immediate, real-world connection inside a beautifully designed facility. Stripping away labels along with their street clothes, patrons navigate a multi-level layout that includes traditional dry saunas, steaming Turkish baths, private cruise cabins, a projection room, and relaxation zones with dark ambient electronic tracks. It is a sex-positive, zero-judgment sanctuary built for pure consensual heat, body freedom, and deep unwinding right in the city center.

changes.name: Klub Kocka
changes.before: Ditch the sleek, commercial tourist traps of the Diocletian's Palace waterfront and plunge directly underground into Klub Kocka. Tucked inside the brutalist concrete basement of the Youth Center (Dom Mladih), this legendary non-profit alternative fortress is run by the Coalition of Youth Associations (KUM). Operating as Split’s absolute capital of raw subculture and electronic rebellion, Kocka strips away all pretension for a beautifully dark, high-octane dreamscape. Depending on the night, you will dance your heart out to heavy Berlin techno, underground drum 'n' bass, industrial punk bands, or hyper-inclusive drag and queer QFest takeovers. It is a sweaty, bass-heavy underground cave built entirely for authentic musical liberation.

changes.name: DIX BAR
changes.before: Welcome to Hell, sis! 🔥 DIX BAR is the absolute epicenter of high-drama, glitter-drenched debauchery right in the beating heart of downtown Mérida. If you are looking to watch local Yucatecan royalty turn the stage upside down, this is your holy grail. The entrance screams a devilish welcome, letting you know exactly what kind of chaotic, gorgeous pop-and-reggaeton fantasy world you have just stepped into. It is chaotic, it is loud, it is sweaty, and the local drag lineup (shoutout to the icons like Candela Yeyé and La Mont) serves face, body, and splits until the lights come up.
changes.after: DIX BAR is a drag-focused bar in central Mérida, with pop and reggaeton in the programme. Local performers take the stage in a loud, late-night setting.

changes.name: Bernardette Show Bar
changes.before: Prepare to have your breath stolen, darling! 🎭 Bernardette Show Bar is Mérida’s premier, ultra-glamorous queer-inclusive cabaret sanctuary tucked neatly away on the iconic Paseo de Montejo. This isn't just a bar; it’s a high-octane theatrical time capsule where old-school Broadway sophistication collides head-on with a dazzling retro fantasy. Boasting an explosive cast of over 15 to 20 spectacular live singers, dancers, and local drag royalty, the venue transforms into a sparkling, neon-lit musical universe.
changes.after: Bernardette Show Bar is a cabaret venue on Paseo de Montejo in Mérida. Live singers, dancers and drag performers present a programme influenced by musical theatre and retro stage shows.

changes.name: La Inventada Cantina
changes.before: Honey, get ready to make a scene because La Inventada Cantina is the ultimate afternoon-to-sunset playground for Mérida’s absolute finest! 💖 Located in the legendary, bright pink "Edificio ROSA JOTISIMX", this spot completely flips the traditional Mexican cantina vibe on its head. It is loud, unapologetically queer, fully air-conditioned, and covered in colorful, eye-popping murals. Instead of waiting until midnight to get your life, La Inventada lets you start day-drinking with the dolls while local drag superstars like Silvana Malvada and Bárbara la Montiel perform high-energy lip syncs right between the tables. It is the perfect place to gossip, scream-sing along to dramatic Latin pop heartbreak anthems, and get delightfully messy before the sun even goes down.
changes.after: La Inventada Cantina is a queer cantina in Mérida's pink Edificio ROSA JOTISIMX. The air-conditioned room has colourful murals and hosts afternoon drinks, Latin pop and drag performances between the tables.

changes.name: Papis
changes.before: Lock eyes and brace yourself, because Papis is where Mérida’s unapologetic, adult-rated late-night fantasy comes alive! ⛓️❤️‍🔥 Far more explicit and uninhibited than standard pop bars, this neon-drenched stronghold is famous for its jaw-dropping, thirst-inducing lineup of muscular Go-Go boys and dancers strutting right across the bar top. From cops and firemen to cowboys, their high-energy themed stripper routines leave absolutely nothing to the imagination. Mix in some sharp-tongued local drag commentary, a pulsating soundtrack of aggressive reggaeton, pop, and regional Mexican bangers, and you have a sweaty, beautifully chaotic den of midnight sin that runs straight through until sunrise.
changes.after: Papis is an adult nightlife venue in Mérida with male dancers, themed strip performances and drag hosting. Reggaeton, pop and regional Mexican music form part of the programme.

changes.name: XOXO Club
changes.before: Clear the runway, bestie, because XOXO Club is serving premium, high-class nightlife realness! 💋✨ Unlike your typical sweaty dive bars, XOXO is the ultimate chic, design-forward sanctuary where Mérida's trendy elite come to slay. Think gorgeous industrial-glam interior aesthetics, stunning chandeliers, metal mesh installations, and a flawless vibe that balances nightclub energy with upscale lounge comfort. The music here is a divine sonic journey—fluctuating between high-fashion girlie pop anthems (Dua Lipa, Gaga, Britney) and heavy reggaeton basslines. Top-tier Drag Race México royalty and killer local icons consistently take the stage, delivering beautifully executed, high-art performances that will leave your jaw on the polished floor.
changes.after: XOXO Club is a Mérida nightclub with chandeliers, metal-mesh installations and an industrial-style interior. Pop and reggaeton accompany performances by local drag artists and guests from Drag Race México.

changes.name: Banana's Club
changes.before: Get ready to peel back your inhibitions, doll, because Banana's Club is Mérida’s ultimate unhinged, wild-child temple of late-night camp! 🍌✨ If you want your nightlife served with a massive side of raucous, sweat-drenched comedy and pure physical spectacle, this is where you drop your anchors. Operated by the infamous "Team Bananas," this legendary spot is a breathless, neon-lit crossover between a high-energy drag theater and a hyper-sexualized adult party.
changes.after: Banana's Club is a Mérida nightlife venue operated by Team Bananas. Its programme combines drag theatre, comedy and adult stage performances in a late-night party setting.

changes.name: Eclipse Cardiff
changes.before: Honey, adjust your wig and get ready to descend into a cellar of pure Welsh camp! Eclipse Cardiff (officially known as Eclipse Cabaret Bar) is the fiercely loved, newly transformed heartbeat of Charles Street's gay strip—occupying the infamous basement vault that used to house Eagle Bar. Since flipping the script, it has evolved into a high-vibe, queer-owned destination where the glitter never settles. By embedding an old-school, intimate cabaret structure into a neon-soaked dance den, it treats Cardiff to non-stop nightly theater.

changes.name: Pulse Cardiff
changes.before: Honey, prepare to enter the absolute mainframe of Welsh queer nightlife. Pulse Cardiff is the massive, shimmering flagship mega-venue anchoring the city's lively Canal Quarter. Having served the community for over two decades, this powerhouse has elevated its game with a massive basement club refit featuring blinding, interactive LED strip lighting arrays, a brand-new DJ cage, and an expanded main stage that has historically hosted pop icons like Charlotte Church and Alexandra Burke. By day, the street level treats you to a relaxed, cozy pub atmosphere serving hearty meals; but when midnight strikes, the bass drops and it transforms into a multi-floor, sweat-drenched pop, EDM, and house music sanctuary. It is big, it is loud, and it is the essential crowning destination for any late-night queer rave in the capital.

changes.name: Solutto Bar
changes.before: If your ideal queer pre-game begins with a killer plate of legendary loaded fries, massive Argentine lomitos, and artisanal cocktails served in a lively, sun-drenched street patio, you drag your crew straight to Solutto Bar. Perfectly situated on the booming high-traffic avenue of the Nueva Córdoba student district, this trendy bar-resto serves up visual delight and culinary fuel. It explicitly skips the stuffy, high-pressure formatting of traditional upscale cocktail lounges, opting instead for a cozy, casual, and highly social neighborhood runway. By day, it functions as a popular retreat for students swapping gossip over rich brunches and iced coffees.

changes.name: Ludwigs Bier und Brot
changes.before: Honey, if you want a venue that bridges the gap between classic German beer tavern realness and a vibrant queer mixer, Ludwigs is serving it on a silver platter! Located right in the thick of the action on Mertensgasse, this cozy, wood-paneled space features a prominent central bar designed for heavy eye contact. It proudly markets itself as a meeting point for both homosexuals and heterosexuals, throwing out judgment and serving up purely chaotic, friendly joy. It is loud, wonderfully packed, and famous for its legendary weekend early-morning breakfast shift that rescues club refugees at dawn.

changes.before: Darlings, if you are exhausted by high-concept cocktail lounges and over-the-top circuit drama, Comeback is your ultimate safe haven. Located on a prominent corner with its entrance wrapping around onto Bismarckstraße, this intimate drinking hole gives pure, unadulterated "Kneipe" nostalgia. It swaps out polished neon and intense strobe lights for dark, traditional furnishings, cozy seating, and a wonderfully relaxed approach to nightlife. It is an easy-going social mixer where you go to slam down cold Kölsch or Altbier, chat up friendly strangers, and listen to familiar pop throwbacks.

changes.before: Bar Studio 1 is Düsseldorf’s effortlessly cool, low-lit jewel box of a cocktail lounge, hidden beneath a vintage vaulted ceiling and beloved for serving premium mixology with a fiercely gay-friendly, inclusive attitude.

changes.name: Clubb 466
changes.before: Located smack in the center of Córdoba capital, this compact, no-nonsense adult bathhouse and cruising enclave swaps modern, slick design gimmicks for raw, vintage masculine heat. It packs a tight, heavy punch across its steam rooms, dry saunas, action darkrooms, video loops, and individual cabins. The venue even flexes its artistic soul by occasionally playing host to interactive erotic photography expos and pop-up installations right inside the steam areas. It is pleasantly retro, fiercely private, highly direct, and stands as a definitive local classic for physical cruising far away from the smartphone tracker apps.

It gives pure classic gay club energy—complete with swirling disco balls, pounding house beats, and unpretentious top-40 remixes. It is loud, it is rowdy, and it is beautifully uninhibited.

changes.name: Europa Disco
changes.before: If you are looking for a glittering, loud, and brilliantly resilient fortress of pure pop trash and drag majesty in the heart of central Argentina, you look for the neon sign of Europa Disco (widely known as Europa Sin Límites). Originally born in 2012 down by the gritty old Mercado de Abasto before migrating to the buzzing student hub of Nueva Córdoba, this iconic multi-room venue has spent well over a decade serving as a massive, unpretentious temple for the local rainbow community. Bypassing generic, snobby club culture entirely, Europa thrives on a wild sonic cocktail of fierce cachengue, aggressive perreo, and classic pop divas, all backdropped by a stellar weekly stage rotation of local drag queens competing in explosive pageants.

changes.name: Club Paraguay
changes.before: If the artistic, rebellious soul of central Argentina decided to build a sprawling, concrete mega-sanctuary for creative misfits, it would manifest exactly as Club Paraguay. Self-declared as a "parallel market of emotions", this massive, 1,000-capacity concert arena and dance hall functions as the beating heart of Córdoba’s cultural explosion. It completely shatters the boring mold of standard commercial discos by operating as an unpretentious, hyper-kinetic crossroads. One night you are pushed against the barrier for cutting-edge indie-rock icons, industrial techno producers, or fierce trap stars, and the next you are caught in a sea of flying glitter during their legendary La Jaleo pop and cachengue takeovers.

changes.name: Housing Club
changes.before: Tucked seamlessly inside downtown Córdoba capital, this venue boldly tears down the boilerplate concept of a generic lounge. It throws out modern posturing to build a high-octane underworld dedicated entirely to sensory freedom and real-world encounters. The layout is an intimate, brilliantly constructed maze divided into three distinct, cinematic tension chambers: an adult video cinema hall, a deep action darkroom maze, and a industrial tunnel, all flanking a beautifully buzzed open-air cocktail patio. It is moody, exceptionally liberating, and functions as the definitive sanctuary for guys who want heavy, dark-electronic soundscapes mixed with absolute physical liberation.

While it plays host to generic electronic and rock events, its flagship alternative techno concepts like Vortex operate as an intense safe haven for Granada's queer clubbers, underground fashionistas, and electronic purists.
