changes.name: OYA Kollektiv CaféKneipe
changes.before: If you are searching for a slice of radical softness, deep intersectional community care, and grassroots political warmth, OYA Kollektiv CaféKneipe is your chosen-family living room. Located under the roof of the legendary Frauenzentrum Schokofabrik in Kreuzberg, this fiercely independent, collectively run safe-haven acts as a vital cultural incubator. The space is brilliantly cozy, lined with community posters and warm lighting, trading typical competitive club preening for genuine human connection. Whether they are hosting intimate indie-folk concerts, chaotic board game nights, or essential solidarity fundraisers, OYA radiates a profound "home away from home" aura where the marginalized are prioritized and celebrated.
changes.after: OYA Kollektiv CaféKneipe is a collectively run café and bar at the Frauenzentrum Schokofabrik in Kreuzberg. Its community programme includes small concerts, board-game nights and solidarity fundraisers.

changes.name: Sofia
changes.before: If you want to experience what Kreuzberg felt like before high-end tech money moved in, Sofia is your gritty, time-traveling retro paradise. This cozy, one-room gay and lesbian neighborhood fixture near Schlesisches Tor is the definition of low-key, soulful old-school Berlin. With its humble, slightly chaotic Bulgarian-themed decor, mismatched vintage furniture, and a cloud of smoke that embraces you at the door, it trades pretentious club line stand-offs for unpretentious, heartwarming hospitality. It functions as a relaxed street-side café by afternoon and a bustling, candlelit local dive by night where you can get a dirt-cheap beer or coffee and engage in actual, deep human conversation.
changes.after: Sofia is a small gay and lesbian neighbourhood bar near Schlesisches Tor in Kreuzberg. Bulgarian-themed decor, vintage furniture and indoor smoking shape the room, which serves coffee by day and drinks in the evening.

changes.name: Pussycat
changes.before: Steeped in queer history and trading high-tech flash for moody, retro allure, Pussycat is one of Schöneberg’s absolute oldest surviving neighborhood institutions. Opened all the way back in 1974 by two women as a dedicated lesbian bar, it has morphed into a legendary, multi-identity time capsule. To get inside, you have to find the subtle entrance and ring the front-door buzzer, a nostalgic throwback to the days when discretion was survival. Once inside, you're greeted by dim red lighting, vintage 60s/70s pub decor, a modest dance floor pumping pop throwbacks, and a cozy, smoke-filled living-room vibe that feels incredibly intimate, welcoming, and delightfully unpolished.
changes.after: Pussycat opened as a lesbian bar in 1974 and now draws a broader crowd in Schöneberg. Entry is by a door buzzer. Inside are red lighting, vintage pub furnishings, a small dance floor and indoor smoking.

changes.name: FLAX Bar
changes.before: If you’ve ever wanted to party inside a wonderfully campy, retro 80s living room complete with cozy sofas, dangling disco balls, and zero techno pretension, FLAX Bar is your destination. Operating since 1994 in Prenzlauer Berg under its legendary owner Steven, this neighborhood classic possesses a classic split personality. During the week, it acts as a relaxed neighborhood café-bar, but once the weekend hits, it shape-shifts into a boisterous mini-club. You won't hear industrial drone beats here; instead, the space is entirely fueled by iconic pop oldies, trashy Schlager classics, lively karaoke sessions, and unadulterated neighborhood joy.
changes.after: FLAX Bar is a Prenzlauer Berg café-bar with sofas and disco balls. Its programme shifts from weekday drinks to busier weekend evenings with pop oldies, Schlager and karaoke.

changes.name: Ashoor Bar
changes.before: If you are looking for an intimate, artistically expressive oasis that blends gritty Friedrichshain subculture with a beautifully warm, cross-cultural heartbeat, Ashoor Bar (previously known to locals as Capture Bar) is the place to be. This cozy, alternative neighborhood gem feels like an underground arts-and-crafts living room where open windows connect directly to the street outside. Under its charismatic owner Ashoor, the space frequently transforms from a low-lit chat lounge into a dynamic cultural hub, hosting everything from vibrant dark disco and electronic DJ nights to raw collage exhibitions and soulful Middle Eastern groove parties.
changes.after: Ashoor Bar, previously listed as Capture, is a small neighbourhood bar in Friedrichshain. Its programme includes electronic DJ nights, Middle Eastern music events and art exhibitions, alongside quieter evenings for drinks.

changes.name: Besenkammer
changes.before: Living up entirely to its literal German translation ("Broom Closet"), Besenkammer is a bite-sized, unapologetic, and completely unpolished piece of East Berlin gay history. Tucked directly beneath the train tracks near Alexanderplatz, this tiny dive holds a legendary 24/7 license. It’s a dark, smoke-filled time capsule where maybe 15 to 30 people can squeeze tightly around a massive wrap-around bar. There is zero industrial techno or modern club elitism here; instead, it blasts classic pop oldies, nostalgic Schlager, and serves up cheap beer while providing front-row seats to the absolute chaotic end-of-the-night human zoo.
changes.after: Besenkammer is a very small gay bar beneath the railway tracks near Alexanderplatz. A wrap-around bar, indoor smoking, pop oldies and Schlager give it a traditional pub setting.

changes.name: BarbieBar
changes.before: If you ever wondered what it would look like if a high-camp drag queen inherited a mid-century salon and painted it entirely in shades of neon bubblegum, BarbieBar is your dream fantasy. Nestled right along the lively Mehringdamm strip in Kreuzberg, this iconic neighborhood cult bar is crammed with hundreds of vintage Barbie dolls swinging from the chandeliers, posed on retro shelving, and arranged in cheeky, staged tableaus across the room. It completely avoids the grim, dark industrial vibe of the city’s techno bunkers, opting instead for pure, unapologetic pink kitsch, delicious signature cocktails, and an outdoor sidewalk terrace that is prime territory for socializing.
changes.after: BarbieBar is a Kreuzberg bar on Mehringdamm decorated with vintage Barbie dolls, pink lighting and retro furniture. It serves cocktails and has a pavement terrace.

changes.name: Curly Bar
changes.before: If you’re tired of trekking all the way to Schöneberg or Neukölln for your queer social fix, Curly Bar is here to claim the crown as the ultimate, cozy neighborhood heart of Wedding. Partially FLINTA*-led, this delightful Antonkiez refuge trades intimidating, heavy techno elitism for radical community warmth, premium house-crafted cocktails, and a living-room layout packed with local art. It functions as a welcoming, low-pressure creative hub during the week and flips into a buzzing community hive on weekends—hosting everything from highly competitive queer chess nights and cozy knitting meetups to emotional, packed karaoke sessions, stand-up comedy, and targeted queer speed dating.
changes.after: Curly Bar is a partially FLINTA*-led neighbourhood bar in Wedding's Antonkiez. It combines cocktails and local art with community events such as chess, knitting, karaoke, comedy and queer speed dating.

changes.name: Triebwerk
changes.before: If you are looking to strip away the glossy pretense of cocktail lounges and dive straight into the raw, unapologetically sleazy underbelly of Berlin’s traditional cruising culture, Club Triebwerk (literally translating to "Engine") is your industrial-strength playground. Tucked away near Hermannplatz on the border of Kreuzberg and Neukölln, this long-standing, men-only sex and fetish institution spans two distinct floors. Up top, it’s a dim, red-lit smoking bar where regulars catch up over cheap pints; downstairs, it transforms into a massive, maze-like action zone equipped with slings, video cabins, a St. Andrew's Cross, and even a clinical examination chair. It is a gritty, raw, and fiercely traditional space where nobody is there to pose—they are there for direct, consensual adult encounters.
changes.after: Triebwerk is a men-only adult venue near Hermannplatz, between Kreuzberg and Neukölln. A smoking bar upstairs connects to a lower-floor cruising area with slings, video cabins and fetish equipment.

changes.name: Böse Buben e.V.
changes.before: If you are looking to escape commercialized corporate mega-clubs and dive straight into raw, heavy-duty underground kink history, Böse Buben e.V. (literally "Bad Boys Club") is your sacred, non-profit community temple. Founded in 1996, this long-running, registered association clubhouse acts as Germany’s absolute premier playground for adult gay men who take their fetishes and S&M seriously. Hidden entirely away inside a secluded backyard courtyard behind an unassuming apartment complex, it traded superficial aesthetic posturing for an incredibly safe, highly educational, and deeply respectful laboratory of sexual freedom.
changes.after: Böse Buben e.V. is a non-profit association founded in 1996, with a courtyard clubhouse for adult gay men's fetish and S&M events. Check the association's current membership and event requirements before attending.

changes.name: Grosse Freiheit 114
changes.before: If you are looking for a place where gritty nautical kitsch meets sex-positive Friedrichshain hedonism, Grosse Freiheit 114 (affectionately dubbed GF114) is your neighborhood beacon. Ditching the polished aesthetics of upscale cocktail lounges, this long-standing institution blends the salty charm of an old-school Hamburg harbor bar with the raw pulse of an underground electronic hangout. Under its refreshed "Queer & Friends" era, it seamlessly balances a cozy front room hosting drag bingo and pub quizzes with a legendary, action-ready cruising darkroom tucked away in the back.
changes.after: Grosse Freiheit 114 is a Friedrichshain bar with nautical decor and electronic music. The listing describes a front room for social events such as drag bingo and quizzes, with a darkroom at the back.

changes.name: Rastlos
changes.before: If you are hunting for the ultimate no-brakes, late-night den where the clock completely ceases to exist, Rastlos (fittingly translating to "Restless") is your final destination. Slotted into the legendary Schöneberg space previously occupied by the infamous Toy-Boy-Bar and Blue Boy Bar, this freshly renovated dive swaps pristine lounge pretense for a gritty, hyper-social playground. Inside, it’s a beautifully unpolished, red-lit cocoon blasting catchy house and pop anthems where local neighborhood regulars, late-night wanderers, and flirty locals collide. It acts as a raw, unpretentious den of old-school Schöneberg cruising culture—where the drinks flow cheap, the conversations are unapologetically forward, and the vibe stays unapologetically wild around the clock
changes.after: Rastlos is a Schöneberg bar in a space previously occupied by Toy-Boy-Bar and Blue Boy Bar. Red lighting, house and pop music frame a late-night setting for drinks and cruising.

changes.name: XXL-Berlin

Operating since 2004 as the absolute largest gay sex cinema and cruising club in the Prenzlauer Berg district, this massive, multi-tiered complex trades casual pub small-talk for uninhibited erotic exploration. Up front, it hosts a brightly lit erotic store open to everyone; but pass the entry desk, and you enter a sprawling 250 m² maze of adult sensory indulgence. Equipped with multiple video cabins, private relaxation cells, a comprehensive darkzone featuring industrial cages and bars, slings, a dedicated "sucking station", and an intense slurp ramp, it serves up pure, unapologetic, and heavy-duty horniness.
changes.after: XXL-Berlin is a gay adult cinema and cruising venue in Prenzlauer Berg. A shop at the front connects to several levels of video cabins, darkrooms and play areas with slings and other fetish equipment.

Far from a polished nightclub, this sprawling outdoor parkland and roadside stretch transforms after dark into a nocturnal wilderness of high-voltage glances and cinematic encounters. It is the ultimate playground for those who prefer their chemistry under the stars, completely free from entry fees, club cards, or closed doors.

Whether you are kicking off your day with an intensely fueled vegan breakfast or settling in for a late-night activist debate, this homey sanctuary effortlessly bridges the gap between radical politics and sublime comfort comfort food.

changes.name: IGOR Libreria
changes.before: Darling, prepare to have your literary and botanical fantasies cross-pollinated. IGOR Libreria is Bologna's ultimate, fiercely independent LGBTQ+ paper sanctuary, completely reimagined for the modern rainbow intellectual. Founded by local icons Raffaele and Luca, it beautifully merges radical queer theory, stunning graphic novels, and underground photography with lush, leafy fronds. It is the cozy, aesthetic community living room where the pages are sharp, the soil is fresh, and the vibe is purely, unapologetically fabulous.

Hosted in a sleek space dripping with 1970s Broadway cinema aesthetics, it seamlessly blends Italy's iconic aperitivo culture with an electric, late-night dance floor where you can be exactly who you want to be.

changes.before: Cascine Park (Parco delle Cascine) is Florence’s ultimate, sprawling open-air playground, serving as a massive, legendary outdoor cruising wilderness hidden under the canopy of the city’s largest public park. Running parallel to the Arno River, this historical woodland shifts gears after dark, transforming its dense tree lines, quiet river paths, and secluded bushes into a thrilling matrix of anonymous, unfiltered nighttime connections, completely free from club fees, association cards, or closed doors.

Breaking away from plastic commercial tourism, this bohemian sanctuary acts as a magnet for the city's progressive literary crowd, wrapping you in the scent of thousands of local and international titles, hanging ivy, and freshly brewed specialty espresso. It's a breathing space where community thrives and where queer lit, independent poetry, and avant-garde art installations find a beautifully curated home.

changes.name: Plus Florence
changes.before: Plus Florence is the city’s ultimate high-energy, budget-luxury playground, redefining the hostel and hotel game with a massive splash of youthful, social energy. Located just steps from Santa Maria Novella, this sprawling urban complex packs an unbelievable punch by pairing budget-friendly shared dorms and private rooms with five-star amenities—think an epic outdoor swimming pool, a steamy Finnish sauna, a Turkish bath, and a panoramic rooftop terrace with jaw-dropping views of the Duomo. It is a vibrant, bustling melting pot where global backpackers, queer solo travelers, and digital nomads link up over cheap pints and sunny terrace vibes.

Small in size but infinitely large in heart, it function as a cozy refuge where colorful locals and global wanderers cross paths. Whether you are sipping on their signature custom-crafted infusions, vibing through a high-voltage drag or cabaret show, or letting loose during an unruly karaoke and dance night, the ambiance is unapologetically warm, fun, and colorful.

Split across high-voltage rooms blasting everything from "Queer Fem Slut Pop" to gritty 2000s indie dance, it’s a sweaty, boundary-free wonderland where drag performance art rules and the only requirement is an appetite for absolute freedom.

changes.name: Q Club

changes.name: Libreria Antigone
changes.before: Listen up, buttercup, because this isn't just a shop—it’s a radical, glitter-dusted intellectual fortress. Libreria Antigone Milano is Milan's premier fiercely independent, transfeminist, and LGBTQIA+ safe-haven bookstore. Named after the classic rebel Antigone—specifically channeling Judith Butler’s queer, anti-state readings—this space is an absolute beacon of counter-cultural resistance right off the bustling fashion strips. It’s a beautiful intersectional matrix where hardcore gender theory rubs shoulders with gorgeous graphic novels, indie zines, and radical poetry. It acts as a thriving community nexus where the patriarchal status quo is shredded page by page, and minds are expanded daily.

changes.name: Anatema
changes.before:
Anatema the Party is Naples’ wildly eccentric, glam-rock queer extravaganza that turns nightlife into a living, breathing theater of beautiful camp subversion. Operating as a traveling community ritual, it seamlessly splits its seasonal personality: hosting dark, high-drama winter club takeovers at the legendary Shine Club before moving outdoors to throw sun-drenched, sandy summer beach raves at Onde Blu Lido. Blasting an unhinged, high-vibe blend of queer pop classics, electronic beats, and trashy Italian disco, it's a sweaty sanctuary where drag divas, club kids, and icons like Cristiano Malgioglio cross paths to celebrate pure, unfiltered self-expression.

changes.name: Parco del Ninfeo

Inside this beloved kitsch paradise, an army of Barbie and Action Men dolls dangle whimsically from the ceiling alongside shimmering disco balls, while vintage black-and-white films flicker softly against exposed brick walls. It is an intimate, wonderfully eccentric bubble of pure queer joy that defies slick modern trends, pairing signature experimental cocktails with feel-good disco anthems for an experience that is effortlessly fabulous and unapologetically playful.

changes.name: Royal Vauxhall Tavern (RVT)
changes.before: The Royal Vauxhall Tavern (RVT) is the undisputed, fierce matriarch of London’s queer performance art, standing proudly as a Grade II-listed Victorian treasure trove of absolute legend. This iconic south London amphitheater of camp has been anchoring the LGBTQ+ community since the post-war era. Bypassing slick, cookie-cutter clubbing, the RVT is a glorious, high-ceilinged, circular temple of joy where the stage is sacred, the pints are refreshingly honest, and the air is thick with decades of radical queer history, world-class cabaret, and unmatched theatrical brilliance.

changes.name: Fire Nightclub
changes.before: Fire Nightclub is an industrial, multi-roomed cavern of late-night hedonism carved directly out of massive Victorian railway arches in Vauxhall. Far from the polite, intimate cabaret spaces of the West End, Fire is a sprawling, high-octane temple of sound and fury that serves as the roaring epicenter of London’s queer after-hours electronic dance scene. Across a subterranean labyrinth of up to ten interconnected arches, the venue unleashes bone-rattling Funktion-One sound systems, immersive laser displays, and pulsing LED light networks. Hosting some of the largest, most legendary circuit, techno, and fetish brands on the planet—including the newly partnered XXL London monthly residencies and the unstoppable Beyond Saturdays—it’s an electric, sweat-soaked playground where the music is intense, the vibes are unapologetically intense, and the party pushes on long into the next morning.

The ground floor hosts a welcoming, neon-hued social lounge where you can chat and devour casual table-side sourdough pizza orders, while the basement morphs into a thumping, sweaty underground sanctuary dedicated to non-curated fringe performance art, avant-garde drag scratch nights, and explosive late-night weekend raves.

Under the gaze of a legendary, glowing neon pink stage heart, the venue discards slick modern nightlife trends to preserve its nostalgic wood-paneled walls, vintage carpets, and cheap pints.

changes.name: La Camionera
changes.before: La Camionera is a sizzling, Mediterranean-inspired slice of East London's "sapphic renaissance" that proudly breaks the mold of cookie-cutter nightlife. A cheeky nod to Spanish slang for "butch lesbian," this beautiful, crowd-funded venue in Hackney stands as the city's only FLINTA-owned and queer-built permanent lesbian sanctuary. Instead of roaring club pop and standard corporate tokenism, it delivers pure continental charm: think sun-dappled, rough plaster walls, hand-painted tiles, a brushed-aluminium bar, and a leafy back garden. By day, it serves up rich espresso and Spanish café culture, before seamlessly dimming the lights for late-night natural wines, vermouth, and artisan tapas.

changes.name: TBPOC-only Trans Sauna
changes.before: Trans Sauna (TBPOC-Only Edition) is a groundbreaking, radical wellness pop-up and biannual sanctuary that completely disrupts the traditionally white, cis-dominated, or heavily commercialized bathhouse landscape. Routinely taking over independent thermal spaces—most notably the subterranean Sauna Social Club in Peckham—this fiercely intentional community initiative is meticulously curated strictly for Black People and People of Colour who identify across the trans+ spectrum (including transgender, non-binary, intersex, and gender non-conforming folks). Stripping away any pressure of the hyper-sexualized cruising scene, it provides a profoundly healing, body-neutral oasis of roaring steam, icy plunges, and low-lit ambient soundtracking where melanin-rich trans bodies are centered, celebrated, and enveloped in collective warmth and absolute restorative rest.

While not explicitly a nightlife venue, this charming neighborhood gem is queer-co-owned and operates as a beautifully welcoming, community-focused sanctuary in Camberwell. Far from a corporate café chain, TOAD is an ultra-creative, flour-dusted temple of seasonal wizardry, celebrated for its wildly innovative, hyper-seasonal pastries, fermented sourdoughs, and unpredictable flavor mashups. It’s a warm, bustling morning hub where the staff are family, the aesthetics are effortlessly stylish, and pastry lovers of all stripes gather to worship at the altar of immaculate lamination.

changes.name: Corner New Cross
changes.before: Corner New Cross is a beautifully curated, architect-designed day-to-night injection of pure intersectional queer joy into South East London. Co-owned by a proudly queer creative duo, this ultra-stylish neighborhood gem breathes new life into a former historic hardware store. By day, it operates as a dreamy, plant-fringed, remote-work sanctuary flooded with natural light and rich artisan espresso. By night, the space dim-lights into a lively cocktail den and a subterranean contemporary art gallery—hosting radical, avant-garde installations like the Trans Rage Exhibition—cementing itself as Lewisham's ultimate, unpretentious cultural playground.

changes.name: The Hoxton Shoreditch
changes.before: The Hoxton hotels are the undisputed pioneers of "open-house" hospitality, elegantly stripping away stiff, old-school luxury to serve up an effortlessly stylish, culturally charged home-away-from-home. While not exclusively LGBTQ+ properties, both the Shoreditch and Holborn outposts are fiercely queer-allied and deeply embedded in London's creative scenes. These design-forward sanctuaries blend industrial-chic architecture with mid-century vintage furnishings, roaring fireplaces, and buzzing, velvet-clad lobby lounges that act as vibrant neighborhood living rooms. They are beautifully inclusive, high-vibe playgrounds where local queer creators, digital nomads, and global travelers drink, work, and sleep under one fabulous, unpretentious roof.

changes.name: Campus Liverpool
changes.before: Campus Liverpool is a roaring, neon-drenched American house-party fantasy that has completely revolutionized the city's Pride Quarter. Taking over the historic former OMG venue in July 2026 under the brilliant direction of legendary local nightlife queen Amy Gwynn (the mastermind behind GBar), this two-story temple of high-octane camp centers itself around the fierce mantra "You Belong Here". The ground floor features "The Front Room" and "Kitchen Disco 2"—a massive, pounding dance floor where everyone inevitably aggregates under a sea of disco balls to scream pop anthems—while the upstairs morphs into "The Living Room," a slightly more relaxed lounge space hosted by a faculty of resident drag "professors". It is a loud, sweat-soaked, Barbie-pink playground designed to feel exactly like the wildest university rager you never want to leave.

changes.name: Navy Bar 2.1
changes.before: Navy Bar 2.1 is a high-octane, neon-drenched pillar of Liverpool's iconic Pride Quarter that has been serving flamboyant late-night energy for decades. Rebranded as Navy Bar 2.1 following a massive £150,000 top-to-bottom transformation in late 2024, this slick, three-story party fortress on Stanley Street bridges old-school gay village history with futuristic nightlife. Beneath state-of-the-art visual rigs and flashing lasers, the multi-level layout includes Navy Social—complete with retro gaming consoles and pool tables—alongside a booming main dance floor flanked by high-rise platforms for bar-top dancers. It is a wildly unpretentious, endlessly fun hub where thumping funky house beats, commercial pop anthems, and spectacular live performers keep the dancefloor packed until the sun comes up.

changes.name: The Benidorm Bar
changes.before: The Benidorm Bar is Liverpool’s ultimate, unapologetic portal to Costa Blanca camp, serving a sunny, high-octane slice of Spanish resort nightlife right in the middle of the chilly Pride Quarter. Bypassing any sense of serious, hyper-polished clubbing, this vibrant Stanley Street oasis is a beautifully loud, neon-lit tribute to package holidays, cheap drinks, and unfiltered seaside joy. Under a canopy of festive decorations and flashing light rigs, the venue functions as an everyday party haven where the energy is deliberately nostalgic, the drinks flow in massive beach buckets, and a phenomenal resident squad of drag hostesses keeps the room in absolute stitches from afternoon until the early hours of the morning.

changes.name: Liverpool Naval Club
changes.before: Liverpool Naval Club is a beautifully unpretentious, community-rooted entertainment bastion that seamlessly pivots from a classic maritime veterans' social lounge into a vibrant, high-energy epicenter for retro music lovers. Located just outside the city center, this brilliantly clean, double-bar neighborhood institution avoids the high-gloss pretense of mainstream commercial venues. Officially designated as an LGBTQ+ friendly and transgender safe space, it serves up a genuinely warm, beautifully multi-generational embrace where legendary local tribute acts, glittery soul-and-Motown revivals, and rowdy weekend bingo nights transform the spacious dancefloors into a zero-judgment zone of pure, budget-friendly joy.

changes.name: Abercromby Square
changes.before: Abercromby Square is the legendary, shadowy crown jewel of Liverpool's late-night urban cruising folklore, tucked discreetly inside the University of Liverpool's historic campus. By day, this grand Georgian square functions as a picturesque academic park where students lunch under leafy canopies. By night, it drops the textbooks to become a highly localized, counter-cultural canvas for anonymous outdoor male encounters. It is a thrillingly unpolished, zero-judgment zone where the architecture is classic, the lighting is intentionally dim, and the codes of silent, spontaneous queer connection have been passed down through generations of local seekers.
changes.after: Abercromby Square is a Georgian square within the University of Liverpool campus. It serves as a daytime park and has a recorded history of outdoor gay cruising. That history does not establish current activity, privacy or safety.

changes.name: Pride Coffee
changes.before: Pride Coffee is Liverpool’s vibrant, ground-breaking crown jewel of daytime queer culture, proudly reigning as the city's only full-time, dedicated LGBTQ+ coffee house and community hub. Elegantly tucked right inside the newly transformed walls of The Navy Bar (the city’s absolute oldest gay venue), this multi-functional haven completely reimagines the Pride Quarter landscape. It strips away late-night club pressures to serve up premium, ultra-affordable artisan hot drinks where every single penny spent directly funds the LCR Pride Foundation to keep Liverpool Pride free for everyone.
changes.after: Pride Coffee is a daytime LGBTQ+ café within Liverpool's Navy Bar. The listing describes a community-hub format in which drink sales support the LCR Pride Foundation.

changes.name: Lovelocks Coffee Shop
changes.before: Lovelocks Coffee Shop is a gorgeous, plant-fringed, fiercely independent oasis of pure community love hidden just behind the iconic World Museum. This proudly queer-owned and female-led neighborhood treasure completely bypasses sterile, corporate café tropes to deliver an incredibly warm, living-room vibe. Adorned with hanging ivy, local indie artwork, and vintage wooden tables, it serves as a crucial daytime sanctuary where spectacular artisan coffees, spectacular homemade vegan cakes, and hearty brunch bowls are served up with a giant side of genuine Scouse hospitality.

changes.name: News From Nowhere
changes.before: This isn't just a place to buy literature; it's a legendary, intersectional stronghold of resistance that has been sticking it to the establishment since 1974. Run entirely as a worker-led, non-hierarchical women’s co-operative, News From Nowhere behaves like the comforting, fiercely political radical bookstore of your dreams. Spanning five stories of absolute counter-culture bliss on the bohemian strip of Bold Street, it acts as a cozy haven where you can deconstruct capitalism, dive into queer liberation history, and pick up local zines under the warm glow of a giant rainbow flag.

changes.name: Club Tropicana
changes.before: Club Tropicana is a loud, unapologetically camp time capsule of pure, cheesy paradise tucked inside the historic Rembrandt complex in the heart of Manchester’s Gay Village. Escaping the heavy basslines of mainstream electronic mega-clubs, this neon-drenched weekend sanctuary unleashes a relentless wave of 80s, 90s, and 00s retro pop anthems, from Wham! to Duran Duran. Adorned with tropical accents and glowing fluorescent lights, it operates as a vibrant, compact haven where a fabulous resident roster of drag queens handle the decks and host chaotic weekend karaoke showdowns, proving that too much glitter is never enough.

changes.name: On Bar Manchester
changes.before: ON Bar Manchester is a sleek, three-story powerhouse of high-energy nightlife anchoring a legendary piece of real estate in the heart of the world-famous Gay Village. Taking over the iconic space once known as Mantos (the venue that originally introduced glass-fronted, open visibility to the village), ON Bar injects the strip with unapologetic, multi-level modern glamour. Ground floor doors open to a bustling Canal Street balcony terrace perfect for daytime sipping, while the upper levels give way to ONTOP—a neon-wrapped pop room, cabaret stages, and a panoramic lounge where high-vibe house house beats and commercial pop anthems keep the dancefloor moving.

changes.name: Bar Pop
changes.before: Bar Pop is a neon-drenched, high-camp sanctuary that serves as one of the most unapologetically fun and theatrically vibrant anchors of Manchester’s Gay Village. Spanning two lively floors on Canal Street, this legendary pop palace totally discards serious club elitism to deliver pure, unfiltered queer joy. changes.name: The Goose
changes.before: The Goose (formerly the iconic Paddy's Goose) is a beautifully down-to-earth, wonderfully attitude-free staple of Manchester’s Gay Village that completely bypasses rigid, high-gloss bar aesthetics. Following a massive, sleek £300,000 top-to-bottom transformation in April 2024, this independent Bloom Street gem successfully preserved its historic, cozy neighborhood pub character while launching a vibrant new era of queer entertainment. It functions as a cheerful, multi-generational safe haven where the craft ales flow, the premium drink deals are always honest, and a fiercely loved resident squad of drag royalty steers a weekly calendar of chaotic quizzes, high-octane karaoke, and packed cabaret showstoppers.

changes.name: Centre Stage
changes.before: Centre Stage is an intimate, high-spirited theatrical jewelry box of pure camp nostalgia tucked discreetly away on a Gay Village side street. Self-described as Manchester's leading venue "Dedicated to Yesteryear", this cozy, wood-trimmed sanctuary completely bypasses thumping electronic club beats to serve up a glorious love letter to old-school showtunes, musical theater favorites, and nostalgic singalongs. It is a glittering escape where you can sip a dazzling drink under the gaze of cinematic legends, belt out a chorus from Wicked, and feel completely, fabulously celebrated.

changes.name: The Thompsons Arms
changes.before: Say hello to the ultimate unpretentious, rough-around-the-edges, independent sanctuary of the Village. Tucked away just off the main Canal Street strip, The Thompsons Arms is a two-floor, no-nonsense queer institution that trades exclusive high-maintenance attitudes for cheap house doubles, absolute camp pop bangers, and zero judgment. It is the kind of beautifully chaotic, time-tested boozer where you can lose track of time over a fiercely competitive round of pool, catch a wildly entertaining drag cabaret act, and dance into the sunrise with a fiercely local crowd.

changes.name: REM Bar
changes.before: Step directly into six decades of pure queer Mancunian heritage. Nestled securely on the corner of Canal Street and Sackville Street, REM Bar is the ultimate, unapologetic cornerstone of the village—completely trading away superficial pretension for real, old-school local pub warmth. It functions beautifully as a dual-natured playground: downstairs is a historic, relaxed community tavern that fiercely champions subcultures like the bear, skin, and leather groups, while upstairs opens up into a high-octane pop showbar packed with drag DJs and nostalgic anthems.

changes.name: The New Union
changes.before: Bow down to the absolute royal matriarch of the Manchester queer scene. Standing proudly on the corner of Princess Street and Canal Street since the 1860s, The New Union is a gorgeous, Grade II listed powerhouse that has been a sanctuary for our community since World War II. This legendary hybrid spot is an beautifully unapologetic cocktail of old-school British pub comfort by day—complete with pool tables and cozy corners—and a high-octane, glitter-drenched showbar by night. It is the premier palace for belt-your-heart-out karaoke, razor-sharp drag cabaret, and late-night dancefloor euphoria where the cheesy pop anthems roll until the sun comes up.

changes.name: Social Refuge / Queer Lit
changes.before: Welcome to the undisputed epicenter of Manchester’s modern queer literary revival. Social Refuge and Queer Lit have joined forces to create an absolute behemoth of an LGBTQ+ sanctuary on the edges of the stylish Ancoats and Northern Quarter neighborhoods. Sprawling out as Europe's largest queer bookstore, this gorgeous, sun-drenched hybrid space seamlessly transitions from a hyper-inclusive co-working coffee house by day into a lively, buzzing community bar and event space by night. It’s a beautifully curated love letter to the community, vibrating with cozy, authentic energy where you can casually nurse a flat white, flip through niche sapphic romances, or clink glasses at an open mic night.

changes.name: The Wee Red Bar
changes.before: Tucked behind a famously sneaky, semi-secret entrance on Lady Lawson Street, The Wee Red Bar is Edinburgh's ultimate indie art-school subculture incubator. Operating out of the Edinburgh College of Art grounds since the early 1980s, this tiny, high-personality box trades slick commercial polish for cheap student union drink prices, sweat-dripping underground live gigs, and pure DIY charm.

changes.name: The Subway Cowgate
changes.before: Forget about sandwiches—this is the ultimate, high-energy basement party bunker that rules Edinburgh's historic Old Town nightlife strip. Tucked snugly right under the colossal stone arches of George IV Bridge, Subway Cowgate is a neon-lit, NYC-subway graffiti-plastered temple of pure, unfiltered pop and cheese. It trades away high-maintenance cocktail snobbery for giant, neon-colored "Venom" slushies, massive throwback anthems, and an electric dance floor where letting go is the only requirement. While it serves up mainstream bangers through the weekend, it transforms into an absolute queer beacon at the start of the week, proving that a basement party is best when it's delightfully loud and beautifully unruly.

changes.name: Bistro Coco
changes.before: Welcome to a slice of pure Parisian indulgence seamlessly woven into the fabric of Edinburgh’s thriving Pink Triangle neighborhood. Helmed by chef Max and his passionate crew, Bistro Coco trades away stuffy white-tablecloth gatekeeping for a wonderfully intimate, low-lit, and romantic haven. Adorned with deep green seating, lush potted plants, and sleek modern touches, it is a culinary sanctuary where you can escape the city noise. Whether you are splitting an indulgent, rich sauce over venison or celebrating over crisp French white wine, this charming neighborhood gem makes elevated dining feel entirely accessible, warm, and beautifully welcoming.

changes.name: R&R Lounge

Tucked neatly into the ground floor of a gorgeous, fully restored 1929 neoclassical building—which doubles as a trendy bed & breakfast upstairs—this whimsical workspace treats brunch like a sacred daily festival. Filled with eclectic ornaments, cozy mismatched seating, and mid-century trinkets, it serves up giant, original culinary daydream plates alongside exceptional specialty coffee.
changes.after: The Caravan Café-Restaurant occupies the ground floor of a restored 1929 building in Thessaloniki, with a bed and breakfast above. Vintage objects, mismatched seating, brunch and speciality coffee shape the café.

changes.name: Egnatia Palace Hotel
changes.before: Egnatia Palace Hotel & Spa is Thessaloniki’s grand, neon-kissed time capsule where 1930s Art Deco opulence flawlessly collides with modern wellness luxury. Housed in one of the city's most visually striking historic buildings right in the beating metropolitan center, this 4-star palace wraps you in an embrace of high aesthetics and velvet-draped nostalgia. It is an absolute dream sanctuary for travelers who want to dive headfirst into the city's chaotic urban energy and then immediately retreat into a subterranean paradise of indoor pools, steam rooms, and pure, indulgent pampering.

changes.name: Backstage Diaries
changes.before: Backstage Diaries is Cologne’s unapologetic, multi-room riot that loudly crowns itself as a beautifully "bitchy queer party". Crashing into the legendary Artheater in the gritty, artsy neighborhood of Ehrenfeld, this long-running 18-year institution acts as a sonic antidote to predictable mainstream gay pop clubs. It ruthlessly shreds the standard scene rulebook by running on an inclusive, open-format ethos where subcultures proudly crash into each other. Spanning across two booming dance floors, the venue layout lets ravers effortlessly plunge down a dark, driving basement techno tunnel before resurfacing into a high-drama main room packed with explosive drag shows, live kink art, and hyper-energetic indie-pop anthems.

changes.name: Kattwinkel Bar & Cafe
changes.before: Kattwinkel Bar & Cafe is one of Cologne’s best-kept, coziest secrets—a charming and warm oasis tucked neatly into the trendy, bohemian Südstadt neighborhood. This is the spot that swaps harsh nightclub neon for plush vintage furniture, muted velvet lighting, and a lovely, slow-paced neighborhood feel. changes.name: Schampanja
changes.before: Schampanja is Cologne’s undisputed, anti-mainstream cult sanctuary that has been proudly giving the middle finger to polished commercial gay clubs since 1985. Affectionately dubbed the "Mother of the Bermuda Triangle," this legendary dive bar trades clinical pop remixes for a loud, unapologetic soundtrack of alternative rock, indie, and raw punk music. The space is intentionally compact, dimly lit, and dripping with historic queer grit—even hosting icons like the Pet Shop Boys and Boy George over its four-decade legacy. It is a delightfully grungy, high-character haven where you can slam cheap glasses of Kölsch under neon shadows and lose yourself in real, unfiltered conversation.

changes.name: Kinkz
changes.before:
KINKZ burst onto the Cologne scene as a thrilling, highly progressive twist on the traditional Schaafenstraße queer strip formula. Breaking away from conventional, strictly old-school setups, this space redefined urban nightlife by launching a hyper-inclusive, fetish-and-cosplay-positive playground built deliberately across all gender lines. Featuring industrial meat-locker textures mixed with dim purple neon lighting and dance cages, it injected a raw, youthful adrenaline rush straight into the city’s subculture. While the brand closed its physical brick-and-mortar storefront on Schaafenstraße, the venue has evolved entirely into a mobile, high-production community machine. They now orchestrate massive, nomadic "Secret Quest" takeovers and pop-up club events at legendary city hot spots like Klub Domhof and The Cage, serving up fierce Eurodance, heavy tech-house, darkrooms, and splash zones.
Obs:  Currently without a fixed permanent location; events bounce across premium Cologne clubs such as Klub Domhof (Hohenzollernbrücke 11, 50667 Cologne, Germany).

changes.name: Na Und
changes.before: Na Und? (literally translating to a cheeky "So What?") is Frankfurt's ultimate, unpretentious vintage time capsule that trades commercial club gloss for the deep, comforting heart of a classic German corner tavern. Tucked slightly off the main Bermuda Triangle bar strip near the courthouse, this long-standing neighborhood institution feels like walking straight into your favorite eccentric uncle’s living room. Complete with a rustic wooden bar counter, an authentic patina vibe, and incredibly fair, recession-proof drink prices, it flips the script on high-attitude nightlife. It is a beautifully relaxed, homey refuge where the music is nostalgic, the draft beer flows fast, and the art of local bar chatter is fiercely preserved.

Furiosa Party is Hamburg’s ultimate, high-octane nomadic sanctuary where explosive Latin American energy and radical queer pride completely take over the dance floor. Originally born as a grassroots movement to carve out space for Latinx queer art and culture, this traveling powerhouse turns traditional European club nights on their head. changes.name: Bar Rendezvous
changes.before: Pouring cheap pints and endless charm onto Müllerstraße since 1999, Bar Rendezvous is Munich’s unapologetic, campy neighborhood dive that completely refuses to grow up. Located a stone's throw from Sendlinger Tor, this unpretentious, pint-sized wonderland swaps out high-concept minimalism for a ceiling dripping in dried flowers and colorful decorations. It is the ultimate low-stakes pre-game pad or high-energy late-night hideout where local daddies, wide-eyed gay youth, and visiting travelers rub shoulders. Expect a steady sonic diet of cheesy Euro-disco, German Schlager hits, and spontaneous dance sessions right up against the front windows.

changes.name: Drei Glöcklein
changes.before: If you are craving a slice of unadulterated queer history served with a side of Bavarian realness, Drei Glöcklein (Three Bells) is the ultimate time machine. Holding the crown as Munich's oldest continuously running gay daytime and evening pub, this wonderfully unassuming sanctuary skips the flashy strobe lights and modern gimmickry in favor of pure, old-school tavern comfort. Tucked away with just a small rainbow flag over the door to hint at the magic inside, its interior delivers cozy, rustic "Hofbräu style" wood paneling and vintage charm.

changes.before: If you are ready to graduate from the casual city bars and dive straight into the deep end of heavy-duty, unadulterated fetish culture, MLC UnderGround is Munich’s undisputed alpha sanctuary. Operated as the private playground for the historic Münchner Löwen Club e.V. (Munich Lion’s Club), this industrial, two-story warehouse wonderland—constructed creatively out of stacked shipping containers—is a relentless, 400-square-meter subculture matrix. It completely leaves vanilla expectations at the door, greeting hardcore hunters with a beautifully equipped gear museum featuring heavy SM rooms, a dedicated "Fistraum", Andrew's crosses, cages, deep-territory slings, a wet area for yellow play, and a massive "fuck area".

changes.name: Englischer Garten
changes.before: If you want to trade the strobe lights for a thrill alfresco, the Englischer Garten serves up Munich’s ultimate, legendary open-air playground. Kimi’s is a hip, converted-garage cocktail den that injects an earthy, soulful vibe into Providence's West End. changes.name: Prospect Terrace Park
changes.before: Perched high above downtown Providence on College Hill, Prospect Terrace Park is a scenic, open-air city overlook that pulls double-duty as a historic landmark and a legendary, quiet nod in the local outdoor gay cruising directory. Anchored by a towering, 15-foot granite statue of Rhode Island's founder Roger Williams (whose actual remains are interred underneath), this compact green space frames a jaw-dropping, panoramic vista of the city skyline and the State House. By day, it’s a tranquil spot for students, locals, and couples to lounge on grassy lawns; after midnight, its dark, elevated shadows historically become a clandestine open-air node for subtle glances and late-night cruising.

Cafe Zoey is a vibrant, cozy boutique crêperie and espresso bar nestled beautifully into Providence's Upper Hope Street on the East Side. Adorned with eclectic decor, a distinct artistic flair, and bright red bistro tables out on the sidewalk, this neighborhood gem serves up hand-flipped sweet and savory crêpes alongside specialized espresso concoctions (like "The Buddy," crafted with Rhode Island's iconic coffee milk). It is an all-welcoming, earth-friendly, and certified Kosher third space where the air is sweet and the hospitality feels like an enthusiastic embrace.

changes.name: The Atlantic House
changes.before: Steeped in legendary queer lore, The Atlantic House (affectionately dubbed the A-House by generations of revelers) is the undisputed grand dame of the American gay nightlife scene. Operating out of a historic 1798 tavern that once served as a creative sanctuary for literary icons like Tennessee Williams and Eugene O'Neill, this multi-room monolith seamlessly bridges revolutionary queer history with high-energy modern hedonism. Whether you are looking to sink into a cozy booth with a cocktail, cruise the upper leather enclave, or sweat it out under the lasers of a packed dance floor, this iconic Cape Cod landmark remains the ultimate beating heart of Provincetown’s uninhibited community spirit.

changes.name: The Paramount
changes.before: As the crowning jewel of the legendary Crown & Anchor complex, The Paramount stands proudly as Provincetown’s largest oceanside dance club. This high-energy waterfront megachurch of queer nightlife features a sprawling dance floor, massive video walls, and a cutting-edge sound system that pumps life right out over the harbor. Serving as the ultimate main stage for iconic drag royalty like Varla Jean Merman and Dina Martina, it morphs seamlessly from a world-class theater space by evening into a sweat-drenched, laser-lit paradise by midnight. If you are looking to lose your mind to international DJs or experience the absolute apex of P-town's festival circuit, this is the grand palace where the music gets turned all the way up.

changes.name: Boatslip Resort (The Deck)
changes.before: Welcome to the absolute spiritual epicentre of daytime queer euphoria: The Boatslip Resort & Beach Club. Perched directly over the shimmering waters of Cape Cod Bay, its massive open-air waterfront deck is home to the world-famous Tea Dance. For decades, this iconic pool-and-patio oasis has served as the ultimate daytime playground where thousands of queer travelers gather under the golden afternoon sun. Driven by the legendary, decades-spanning house beats of resident DJ Maryalice, the space transforms everyday at the stroke of four into a beautifully chaotic sea of singing, dancing, and high-energy mingling. If you haven't held a Planter's Punch plastic cup while bouncing to classic anthems on this colossal wooden deck, you haven't truly experienced Provincetown.

Established in 1997 by local icon Lori Kline, this bright and bustling Jewish-deli-meets-beachside-bistro is the perfect place to "plotz" after a wild night out or a long morning on Poodle Beach. changes.name: The Answer Brewpub
changes.before: Pouring out pure liquid joy and community-first hospitality on West Broad Street, The Answer Brewpub serves as Richmond’s ultimate, ground-breaking destination where boundary-pushing craft beer meets authentic Vietnamese flavor. Founded by local culinary legend and James Beard semi-finalist An Bui as RVA’s very first Asian-owned craft brewery, this vibrant 12,000-square-foot adult sandbox functions as a lively extension of the iconic Mekong restaurant next door. Ditching stuffy corporate brewery vibes for a colorful setup complete with a retro arcade, a dedicated live music stage, and a jaw-dropping 56+ rotating tap system, it is most famous for its cult-favorite "Joose" fruited sours, heavy barrel-aged stouts, and legendary "Andall" infusions.

changes.before: Ditching the neon-soaked bar rooms for a completely raw, sun-dappled oasis of wilderness connection, the Texas Beach trails within the James River Park System offer Richmond’s ultimate, historic outdoor cruiser experience. Tucked away along the river's rugged northern banks beneath lush tree canopies and dramatic, colorful train trestle murals, this secluded dirt path and sandy escape has long functioned as a secret, offline meeting ground for free spirits. It is an adventurous, thoroughly unshielded slice of nature where passing glances on wooden footbridges, sunbathing on massive granite rocks, and hidden river pathways skip the smartphone algorithms entirely—keeping Richmond’s classic, countercultural cruising heritage alive right beside the rushing rapids.
